Textbook Question · Problem 23
Search and rescue teams work to find lost hikers. Members of the search team separate and walk parallel to one another through the area to be searched. Table 1.5 shows the percent, P, of lost individuals found for various separation distances, d, of the searchers.
Separation distance d (ft)20406080100
Approximate percent found, P9080706050
a. Explain how you know that the percent found, P, could be a linear function of separation distance, d.
A. For every 20 ft increase in d, P decreases by 10 (constant difference)
B. P is always greater than d, and both are positive numbers
C. For every 20 ft increase in d, P decreases by more each time
D. For every 20 ft increase in d, P is halved (constant ratio)

A. For every 20 ft increase in d, P decreases by 10 (constant difference)

For every 20 ft increase in d, P decreases by 10: the differences are constant, so P could be linear in d.

Look at the change in P each time d goes up by 20.

b. Find P as a linear function of d.
A. P = 100 − 10d
B. P = 100 − 2d
C. P = 90 − 0.5d
D. P = 100 − 0.5d

D. P = 100 − 0.5d

m = −10/20 = −0.5. P − 90 = −0.5(d − 20) → P = −0.5d + 10 + 90 = 100 − 0.5d.

The slope is −10 over 20.

c. What is the slope of the function? Give units and interpret the answer.
A. −0.5 percent per foot: each extra foot of separation lowers the percent found by 0.5
B. −10 percent per foot: each extra foot lowers the percent found by 10
C. 0.5 percent per foot: each extra foot raises the percent found by 0.5
D. −0.5 feet per percent: each extra percent lowers the distance by 0.5 ft

A. −0.5 percent per foot: each extra foot of separation lowers the percent found by 0.5

Slope = −0.5 percent per foot: each extra foot of separation lowers the percent of lost people found by 0.5.

Units of slope = percent over feet.

d. What are the vertical and horizontal intercepts of the function? Give units and interpret the answers.
A. Vertical: 90% (searchers side by side); horizontal: d = 180 ft (nobody is found)
B. Vertical: 100% (nobody is found); horizontal: d = 200 ft (everyone is found)
C. Vertical: 100% (searchers side by side); horizontal: d = 200 ft (nobody is found)
D. Vertical: 200 ft (searchers side by side); horizontal: P = 100% (nobody is found)

C. Vertical: 100% (searchers side by side); horizontal: d = 200 ft (nobody is found)

d = 0 → P = 100%: when the searchers walk side by side, everyone is found. P = 0 → 0.5d = 100 → d = 200 ft: at 200 ft apart, nobody is found.

Vertical: put d = 0. Horizontal: put P = 0.

D. w = 5h − 174; slope 5 inches per pound

m = 5 lb/inch. w − 166 = 5(h − 68) → w = 5h − 340 + 166 = 5h − 174.

Use the point (68, 166) in point-slope form.

c. Find height, h, as a linear function of weight, w. What is the slope of the line? What are the units for the slope?

B. h = 0.2w + 34.8; slope 0.2 pounds per inch

D. h = 0.2w + 68; slope 0.2 inches per pound

Textbook Question · Problem 32

Maximum heart rate (MHR), in beats per minute, a = age in years: Females: MHR = 226 − a, Males: MHR = 220 − a.

Experiments suggest that the female MHR decreases by 12 beats per minute by age 21, and by 19 beats per minute by age 33. Is this consistent with MHR being approximately linear with age?
A. Yes, the rates are almost equal (12/21 ≈ 0.57 and 19/33 ≈ 0.58)
B. No, because MHR increases with age
C. No, the rates are very different (12/21 ≈ 0.57 and 19/33 ≈ 0.79)

A. Yes, the rates are almost equal (12/21 ≈ 0.57 and 19/33 ≈ 0.58)

12/21 ≈ 0.57 and 19/33 ≈ 0.58 beats per minute per year. The rates are almost the same, so it is consistent with an approximately linear function.

Linear = about the same rate at both ages.

9/21 ≈ 0.43 and 26/33 ≈ 0.79. The rates are very different, so it is not consistent with MHR being approximately linear.

Lecture 3Average Rate of Change and Relative Change (1.3)

10 lecture · 50 textbook · 2 past exam questions

1. Average Rate of Change from Tables & Data2. Average Rate of Change from Graphs & Formulas3. Relative Change & Relative Rate of Change4. Increasing, Decreasing & Concavity5. Average Velocity
📖 شرح المحاضرة — Average Rate of Change and Relative Change (1.3)

الشرح فيه 5 أجزاء، بنفس ترتيب الأسئلة تحت. اقري الجزء، وبعدين حلي أسئلته. الفكرة الكبيرة: كم الشي تغير، وبأي سرعة؟

1️⃣ متوسط معدل التغير من الجداول (Average Rate of Change from Tables & Data)

التغير (Change) = القيمة الأخيرة − القيمة الأولى. بس.

متوسط معدل التغير (Average Rate of Change = ARC) = التغير مقسوم على الزمن. يعني كم يتغير الشي كل سنة (أو كل وحدة) بالمتوسط. مثل سرعة السيارة: كم كيلو قطعتي ÷ كم ساعة 🚗.

ARC = (f(b) − f(a)) / (b − a) = Δy / Δx
  • نفس قانون الميل (Slope) اللي أخذناه في المحاضرة 2
  • الوحدة = وحدة y ÷ وحدة x، مثلاً inch/year
  • ARC موجب ← الشي يزيد 📈، ARC سالب ← الشي ينقص 📉
🔑 التفسير (Interpret): "بين سنة a وسنة b، الـ [الشي] زاد/نقص بمقدار |ARC| [وحدة] كل سنة (بالمتوسط)".
مثال (Ex 1): ارتفاع القفز بالزانة (إنش) بالأولمبياد

i. بين 1960 و 1968:

ARC = (213 − 185) / (1968 − 1960) = 28 / 8
ARC = 3.5 inch/year

وبين 1992 و 2000:

ARC = (232 − 228) / (2000 − 1992) = 4 / 8
ARC = 0.5 inch/year

ii. وين زاد أسرع؟ اللي الـ ARC حقه أكبر:

1960–1968, because 3.5 > 0.5
مثال (Ex 2): إنتاج التبغ بأمريكا (مليون باوند)

i. بين 2003 و 2010. خذي بس أول رقم وآخر رقم (الأرقام اللي بالنص ما تدخل):

ARC = (719 − 802) / (2010 − 2003) = −83 / 7
ARC ≈ −11.86 million pounds/year

يعني الإنتاج نقص تقريباً 11.86 مليون باوند كل سنة. (بالملزمة مكتوب −11.84، بس الحساب الصحيح −11.86)

ii. في فترة كان ARC فيها موجب؟ دوري وين الأرقام تزيد:

2003 → 2004: 802 → 882 ↗
2005 → 2009: 645 → 728 → 788 → 801 → 823 ↗
Yes: 2003–2004 and 2005–2009

مثلاً ARC = (882 − 802)/(2004 − 2003) = 80 million pounds/year.

2️⃣ متوسط معدل التغير من الرسم والمعادلة (Average Rate of Change from Graphs & Formulas)
  • من الرسم: اقري قيمة y عند البداية والنهاية من المنحنى، وبعدين نفس القانون
  • من المعادلة: عوضي a و b في الدالة عشان تطلعين f(a) و f(b)
🔑 الخط القاطع (Secant line) = خط مستقيم يوصل بين نقطتين على المنحنى.
الـ ARC بين a و b = ميل الخط القاطع اللي يوصل (a, f(a)) و (b, f(b)).
مثال (Ex 3): عدد المزارع بأمريكا (مليون) من الرسم، بين 1950 و 1970

من الرسم: سنة 1950 ← تقريباً 5.4، وسنة 1970 ← تقريباً 2.8:

ARC = (2.8 − 5.4) / (1970 − 1950) = −2.6 / 20
ARC = −0.13 million farms/year

يعني عدد المزارع نقص 0.13 مليون (يعني 130,000 مزرعة) كل سنة.

مثال (Ex 4): f(x) = √x بين x = 1 و x = 4

(a) أول شي طلعي القيمتين:

f(1) = √1 = 1 ; f(4) = √4 = 2
ARC = (f(4) − f(1)) / (4 − 1) = (2 − 1) / 3
ARC = 1/3 ≈ 0.33

(b) الـ ARC هو ميل الخط اللي يوصل بين النقطتين على الرسم:

The secant line through (1, 1) and (4, 2)
3️⃣ التغير النسبي ومعدل التغير النسبي (Relative Change & Relative Rate of Change)

أحياناً التغير لحاله ما يكفي. نقص 23$ من بنطلون 75$ شي كبير، بس نقص 23$ من سيارة 20,000$ ولا شي! عشان جذي نقيس التغير نسبةً للبداية.

RC = (new − old) / old
  • التغير النسبي (Relative Change = RC)، ويسمونه التغير المئوي (Percent change)
  • دايماً نقسم على القيمة القديمة (الأولى)
  • الجواب عشري، اضربيه × 100 عشان يصير %
RRC = ARC / f(a)
  • معدل التغير النسبي (Relative Rate of Change = RRC) = كم % يتغير كل سنة
  • f(a) = القيمة في بداية الفترة
  • الوحدة: % per year (أو per day …)
مثال (Ex 5): بنطلون سعره 75.99$ صار بالتخفيض 52.99$. التغير النسبي؟
RC = (52.99 − 75.99) / 75.99
RC = −23 / 75.99 ≈ −0.303
RC ≈ −30.3%

السالب يعني نقص، يعني الخصم تقريباً 30%.

مثال (Ex 6): RRC لعدد المزارع بين 1950 و 1970 (نفس رسم Ex 3)

من Ex 3 عندنا ARC = −0.13، والقيمة بالبداية (1950) = 5.4:

RRC = ARC / f(1950) = −0.13 / 5.4
RRC ≈ −0.0241
RRC ≈ −2.41% per year

يعني المزارع نقصت تقريباً 2.41% كل سنة.

مثال (Past exam 2024 Q1): مساحة الجرح A (mm²) كل 5 أيام

a. ARC بين يوم 10 (140) ويوم 25 (95):

ARC = (95 − 140) / (25 − 10) = −45 / 15
ARC = −3 mm²/day: the wound area decreases by 3 mm² per day

b. RRC = ARC ÷ القيمة بالبداية (يوم 10):

RRC = −3 / 140 ≈ −0.0214
RRC ≈ −2.14% per day: the area decreases by about 2.14% per day
مثال (Past exam 2022 Q1): حالات سرطان البنكرياس 27000 سنة 1997، و 31860 سنة 2004

a. ARC (لاحظي إن رقم 2002 ما نحتاجه):

ARC = (31860 − 27000) / (2004 − 1997) = 4860 / 7
ARC ≈ 694.3 cases/year: cases increased by about 694 per year

b. RRC:

RRC = 694.3 / 27000 ≈ 0.0257
RRC ≈ 2.57% per year: cases increased by about 2.57% per year
4️⃣ التزايد والتناقص والتقعر (Increasing, Decreasing & Concavity)

التزايد والتناقص: اقري الرسم من اليسار لليمين. طالع ↗ = يتزايد (Increasing). نازل ↘ = يتناقص (Decreasing).

التقعر (Concavity) = انحناء الرسم، وين الانحناء "يفتح":

النوعالشكليعني
مقعر للأعلى
Concave up		∪ 😊مثل الكوب، يمسك ماي. معدل التغير يزيد
مقعر للأسفل
Concave down		∩ ☹️مثل الخيمة، الماي يطيح. معدل التغير ينقص
ولا وحدةخط مستقيممعدل التغير ثابت (خطي)
🔑 الأربع حالات:
↗ + ∪ = يزيد ويسرع (Increasing, concave up)
↗ + ∩ = يزيد بس يبطّئ (Increasing, concave down)
↘ + ∪ = ينقص بس يبطّئ النزول (Decreasing, concave up)
↘ + ∩ = ينقص ويسرع النزول (Decreasing, concave down)
مثال (Ex 7): من الرسم، وين الدالة تزيد/تنقص، ووين مقعرة للأعلى/للأسفل؟

(a) تابعي المنحنى: يطلع لين x = 2، ينزل من 2 لين 6، وبعدين يطلع مرة ثانية:

Increasing: x < 2 and x > 6 ; Decreasing: 2 < x < 6

(b) شوفي شكل الانحناء: قبل x = 4 شكله خيمة ∩، وبعدها شكله كوب ∪:

Concave down: x < 4 ; Concave up: x > 4
مثال (Ex 8): أزواج النقاط A إلى I على الرسم

لكل زوج نقاط ورا بعض اسألي سؤالين: ① طالع ولا نازل؟ ② الانحناء ∪ ولا ∩؟

i. ↗ + ∪ → D–E and H–I
ii. ↗ + ∩ → A–B and E–F
iii. ↘ + ∪ → C–D and G–H
iv. ↘ + ∩ → B–C and F–G
i. D–E, H–I   ii. A–B, E–F   iii. C–D, G–H   iv. B–C, F–G
💡 من جدول (بدون رسم): احسبي الـ ARC بين كل نقطتين ورا بعض.
الـ ARC قاعد يكبر ← مقعر للأعلى ∪. قاعد يصغر ← مقعر للأسفل ∩. ثابت ← خطي.
مثال (Ex 9): جدول f(t)، و t تزيد 5 كل مرة

(i) القيم تزيد من 12.6 لين 42.7:

Increasing

(ii) نحسب ARC بين كل نقطتين:

(13.1 − 12.6)/5 = 0.1
(14.1 − 13.1)/5 = 0.2
(16.2 − 14.1)/5 = 0.42
(20.0 − 16.2)/5 = 0.76
(29.6 − 20.0)/5 = 1.92
(42.7 − 29.6)/5 = 2.62

الـ ARC قاعد يكبر (0.1 ← 2.62)، يعني يزيد ويسرع:

Concave up
5️⃣ متوسط السرعة (Average Velocity)

متوسط السرعة (Average velocity) = نفس الـ ARC، بس لـالمكان أو الارتفاع مع الزمن.

v = (s(b) − s(a)) / (b − a)
  • موجب ← الشي يتحرك لفوق (أو يبعد)
  • سالب ← الشي يتحرك لتحت (أو يقرب)
  • الوحدة: وحدة المسافة ÷ وحدة الزمن، مثلاً ft/sec
مثال (Ex 10): ارتفاع الجريب فروت y (قدم) بعد ما انرمى لفوق، من t = 4 لين t = 6

من الجدول: y(4) = 150 و y(6) = 30:

v = (30 − 150) / (6 − 4) = −120 / 2
v = −60 ft/sec

سالب لأن الارتفاع قاعد ينقص، يعني الجريب فروت قاعد يطيح لتحت.

⚠️ أخطاء شائعة
❌ تقسمين الـ RC على القيمة الجديدة ← ✅ دايماً على القيمة القديمة (الأولى).
❌ في RRC تقسمين على القيمة الأخيرة ← ✅ تقسمين الـ ARC على قيمة بداية الفترة.
❌ تستخدمين أرقام النص في ARC ← ✅ بس أول وآخر نقطة بالفترة.
❌ تنسين الإشارة السالبة ← ✅ السالب معناه نقص، ولازم يبين بالجواب والتفسير.
❌ تنسين الوحدة ← ✅ ARC: وحدة y/وحدة x. RRC: % per وحدة x.
🧠 كيف تعرفين نوع السؤال؟
إذا السؤال فيه…سوي
"change" بسnew − old
"average rate of change" / "ARC"(f(b) − f(a)) / (b − a)
"which period increased faster"قارني الـ ARC، الأكبر أسرع
"any interval where ARC was positive"دوري وين الأرقام تزيد ورا بعض
"represent ARC as slope of a line"الخط القاطع (Secant line) بين النقطتين
"relative change" / "percent change"(new − old) / old × 100%
"relative rate of change" / "RRC"ARC / f(a)
"increasing / decreasing"طالع ↗ ولا نازل ↘
"concave up / down" من رسمكوب ∪ ولا خيمة ∩
"concave up / down" من جدولاحسبي ARC المتتالية: تكبر ∪، تصغر ∩
"average velocity"نفس ARC للمكان، وفسري الإشارة

✍️ جربي حلي الأسئلة تحت بزر Solve here، والحسابات بتطلع لك على طول.

1. Average Rate of Change from Tables & Data

2 lecture · 14 textbook questions

Lecture Question · Ex 1
The table shows the height of the winning pole vault at the Olympics during the 1960s and 1990s. Winning height in men's Olympic pole vault (approximate):
Year196019641968…199219962000
Height (inches)185201213…228233232
i. Find the rate of change of the winning height between 1960 and 1968, and between 1992 and 2000.
A. 1960–1968: 28 in/year; 1992–2000: 4 in/year
B. 1960–1968: 0.5 in/year; 1992–2000: 3.5 in/year
C. 1960–1968: 4 in/year; 1992–2000: 0.6 in/year
D. 1960–1968: 3.5 in/year; 1992–2000: 0.5 in/year

D. 1960–1968: 3.5 in/year; 1992–2000: 0.5 in/year

ARC = (213 − 185)/(1968 − 1960) = 28/8 = 3.5 inch/year. ARC = (232 − 228)/(2000 − 1992) = 4/8 = 0.5 inch/year.

Change in height ÷ change in years.

ii. In which of these two periods did the height increase faster?
A. 1960–1968, because its ARC is larger
B. 1992–2000, because the heights are larger
C. Both periods increased at the same rate
D. 1992–2000, because its ARC is larger

A. 1960–1968, because its ARC is larger

Since ARC₁ (3.5) is larger than ARC₂ (0.5), the height increased faster in the first period (the 1960s).

Larger ARC = faster increase.

Lecture Question · Ex 2
Similar problem (different numbers): Textbook Problem 24
The table below shows the production of tobacco in the US (millions of pounds).
Year2003200420052006
Production802882645728
Year2007200820092010
Production788801823719
i. What is the average rate of change (ARC) in tobacco production between 2003 and 2010? Give units and interpret your answer in terms of tobacco production.
A. ≈ −83 million pounds/year: production decreased by 83 million pounds per year
B. ≈ 11.86 million pounds/year: production increased by about 11.86 million pounds per year
C. ≈ −11.86 million pounds/year: production decreased by about 11.86 million pounds per year
D. ≈ −10.38 million pounds/year: production decreased by about 10.38 million pounds per year

C. ≈ −11.86 million pounds/year: production decreased by about 11.86 million pounds per year

ARC = (719 − 802)/(2010 − 2003) = −83/7 ≈ −11.86 million pounds/year. Tobacco production decreased by about 11.86 million pounds per year between 2003 and 2010. (Note: the lecture notes write −11.84; −83/7 = −11.857 ≈ −11.86.)

Use only the first and last values.

ii. During this seven-year period, is there any interval during which the average rate of change was positive? If so, when?
A. No, the ARC was always negative
B. Yes: 2003–2004 and 2005–2009
C. Yes: 2003–2004 only
D. Yes: 2004–2005 and 2009–2010

B. Yes: 2003–2004 and 2005–2009

The ARC was positive during 2003–2004 (802 → 882) and 2005–2009 (645 → 728 → 788 → 801 → 823). E.g. ARC = (882 − 802)/(2004 − 2003) = 80 million pounds/year.

Positive ARC = the value went up.

Textbook Question · Problem 17

2. Average Rate of Change from Graphs & Formulas

2 lecture · 7 textbook questions

Lecture Question · Ex 3
Use the given figure to estimate the average rate of change (ARC) of the number of farms in the US between 1950 and 1970.
ARC = ?
A. 0.13 million farms/year
B. −0.024 million farms/year
C. −0.13 million farms/year
D. −2.6 million farms/year

C. −0.13 million farms/year

ARC = (2.8 − 5.4)/(1970 − 1950) = −2.6/20 = −0.13 million farms/year. The number of farms in the US decreased by 0.13 million (130,000) farms per year.

Read the two points, then rise ÷ run.

Lecture Question · Ex 4
f(x) = √x
(a) Find the average rate of change (ARC) of y = f(x) = √x between x = 1 and x = 4.
A. 1
B. 1/3 ≈ 0.33
C. 3
D. 2/3 ≈ 0.67

B. 1/3 ≈ 0.33

ARC = (f(4) − f(1))/(4 − 1) = (2 − 1)/3 = 1/3 ≈ 0.33.

√4 = 2 and √1 = 1.

(b) Graph f(x) and represent this average rate of change as the slope of a line. Which line is it?
A. The tangent line at (4, 2)
B. The horizontal line y = 1/3
C. The secant line through (1, 1) and (4, 2)
D. The secant line through (1, 1) and (4, 16)

C. The secant line through (1, 1) and (4, 2)

The ARC is the slope of the secant line joining the points (1, f(1)) = (1, 1) and (4, f(4)) = (4, 2).

ARC = slope of the secant line between the two points.

Textbook Question · Problem 12
f(x) = 2x²
Find the average rate of change of f(x) = 2x² between x = 1 and x = 3.
A. 16
B. 4
C. 9
D. 8

D. 8

f(1) = 2, f(3) = 18. ARC = (18 − 2)/(3 − 1) = 16/2 = 8.

Find f at both ends first.

Textbook Question · Problem 13
f(x) = 3x² + 4
ARC Find the average rate of change of f(x) = 3x² + 4 between x = −2 and x = 1.
A. −3
B. 3
C. −1
D. −9

A. −3

f(−2) = 3(4) + 4 = 16, f(1) = 3 + 4 = 7. ARC = (7 − 16)/(1 − (−2)) = −9/3 = −3.

1 − (−2) = 3.

Graph Illustrate your answer graphically. The ARC is the slope of which line?
A. The secant line through (−2, 7) and (1, 16)
B. The tangent line at (1, 7)
C. The secant line through (−2, 16) and (1, 7)
D. The secant line through (−2, 4) and (1, 4)

C. The secant line through (−2, 16) and (1, 7)

The ARC = −3 is the slope of the secant line joining (−2, 16) and (1, 7) on the graph of f(x) = 3x² + 4.

Join the two points of the graph.

Textbook Question · Problem 14
When a deposit of $1000 is made into an account paying 8% interest, compounded annually, the balance, $B, in the account after t years is given by B = 1000(1.08)ᵗ.
Find the average rate of change in the balance over the interval t = 0 to t = 5. Give units and interpret your answer in terms of the balance in the account.
A. ≈ 469.33 dollars/year: the balance grows by about $469.33 per year
B. ≈ 293.87 dollars/year: the balance grows by about $293.87 per year
C. ≈ 80 dollars/year: the balance grows by $80 per year
D. ≈ 93.87 dollars/year: the balance grows by about $93.87 per year

D. ≈ 93.87 dollars/year: the balance grows by about $93.87 per year

B(5) = 1000(1.08)⁵ ≈ 1469.33; B(0) = 1000. ARC = (1469.33 − 1000)/5 ≈ 93.87 dollars/year.

Calculate B(5) first.

Textbook Question · Problem 18
Figure 1.34 shows the total value of US imports, in billions of dollars.
a. Was the value of the imports higher in 1985 or in 2003? Approximately how much higher?
A. 2003, higher by ≈ 51 billion dollars
B. 2003, higher by ≈ 920 billion dollars
C. 2003, higher by ≈ 1,260 billion dollars
D. 1985, higher by ≈ 920 billion dollars

B. 2003, higher by ≈ 920 billion dollars

Imports were about 340 billion dollars in 1985 and about 1,260 billion dollars in 2003: 2003 was higher by ≈ 920 billion dollars.

Read both ends of the graph.

b. Estimate the average rate of change of US imports between 1985 and 2003. Give units and interpret your answer in terms of imports.
A. ≈ 51 billion dollars/year: imports increased by about 51 billion dollars per year
B. ≈ −51 billion dollars/year: imports decreased by about 51 billion per year
C. ≈ 70 billion dollars/year: imports increased by about 70 billion per year
D. ≈ 920 billion dollars/year: imports increased by about 920 billion per year

A. ≈ 51 billion dollars/year: imports increased by about 51 billion dollars per year

ARC ≈ 920/(2003 − 1985) = 920/18 ≈ 51 billion dollars/year.

Divide by 18 years.

Textbook Question · Problem 31
Figure 1.7 in Problem 14 of Section 1.1 shows the amount of nicotine N = f(t), in mg, in a person's bloodstream as a function of the time, t, in hours, since the last cigarette.
a. Is the average rate of change in nicotine level positive or negative? Explain.
A. Positive, because nicotine is increasing
B. Zero, because the graph levels off
C. Negative, because nicotine is decreasing
D. Positive, because the graph is concave up

C. Negative, because nicotine is decreasing

The nicotine level decreases over time, so the average rate of change is negative.

Decreasing → negative.

b. Find the average rate of change in the nicotine level between t = 0 and t = 3. Give units and interpret your answer in terms of nicotine.
A. ≈ −0.087 mg/hour: nicotine decreased by about 0.087 mg per hour
B. ≈ −0.26 mg/hour: nicotine decreased by about 0.26 mg per hour
C. ≈ −0.047 mg/hour: nicotine decreased by about 0.047 mg per hour
D. ≈ 0.087 mg/hour: nicotine increased by about 0.087 mg per hour

A. ≈ −0.087 mg/hour: nicotine decreased by about 0.087 mg per hour

ARC = (f(3) − f(0))/3 ≈ (0.14 − 0.4)/3 = −0.26/3 ≈ −0.087 mg/hour. (If f(3) is read as 0.15, ARC ≈ −0.083 mg/hour; either way about −0.08 to −0.09.)

f(0) = 0.4 mg.

Textbook Question · Problem 34
Problems 34–35 refer to Figure 1.38, which shows the contraction velocity of a muscle as a function of the load it pulls against.
a. In terms of the muscle, interpret the vertical intercept.
A. 0 cm/sec: the velocity with no load
B. 30 cm/sec: the contraction velocity with no load
C. 4 kg: the load at which the muscle cannot contract
D. 30 kg: the largest load the muscle can pull

B. 30 cm/sec: the contraction velocity with no load

Vertical intercept = 30 cm/sec: the contraction velocity when there is no load.

Load = 0.

b. In terms of the muscle, interpret the horizontal intercept.
A. 4 cm/sec: the slowest contraction velocity
B. 1 kg: the load that halves the velocity
C. 30 cm/sec: the contraction velocity with no load
D. 4 kg: the load at which the muscle cannot contract

D. 4 kg: the load at which the muscle cannot contract

Horizontal intercept = 4 kg: the load at which the contraction velocity is zero (the muscle cannot contract).

Velocity = 0.

Textbook Question · Problem 35
Use Figure 1.38 (contraction velocity of a muscle against load).
(a) Find the change in muscle contraction velocity when the load changes from 1 kg to 3 kg. Give units.
A. ≈ −22 cm/sec
B. ≈ −11 cm/sec
C. ≈ −5.5 cm/sec
D. ≈ 11 cm/sec

B. ≈ −11 cm/sec

Velocity ≈ 14 cm/sec at 1 kg and ≈ 3 cm/sec at 3 kg. Change ≈ 3 − 14 = −11 cm/sec.

Final − initial.

(b) Find the average rate of change in the contraction velocity between 1 kg and 3 kg. Give units.
A. ≈ −5.5 (cm/sec)/kg
B. ≈ −11 (cm/sec)/kg
C. ≈ −3.7 (cm/sec)/kg
D. ≈ 5.5 (cm/sec)/kg

A. ≈ −5.5 (cm/sec)/kg

ARC ≈ −11/(3 − 1) = −5.5 (cm/sec) per kg.

Divide the change by 2 kg.

3. Relative Change & Relative Rate of Change

2 lecture · 13 textbook · 2 past exam questions

Lecture Question · Ex 5
Find the relative change (RC) in the price of a $75.99 pair of jeans if the sale price is $52.99.
RC = ?
A. ≈ −0.434 = −43.4%
B. ≈ 0.303 = 30.3%
C. ≈ −0.303 = −30.3%
D. ≈ −23 = −2300%

C. ≈ −0.303 = −30.3%

RC = (52.99 − 75.99)/75.99 = −23/75.99 ≈ −0.303 = −30.3%. The discount in the price is about 30%.

Divide the change by the ORIGINAL price.

Lecture Question · Ex 6
Use the given figure to estimate the relative rate of change (RRC) of the number of farms in the US between 1950 and 1970.
RRC = ?
A. ≈ −4.6% per year
B. ≈ −0.13% per year
C. ≈ 2.4% per year
D. ≈ −2.4% per year

D. ≈ −2.4% per year

From Ex 3, ARC = −0.13 million/year. RRC = ARC/f(1950) = −0.13/5.4 ≈ −0.0241 = −2.41% per year. The number of farms decreased by about 2.41% per year.

RRC = ARC ÷ original value.

Textbook Question · Problem 5
In Problems 5–8, find the relative, or percent, change.
S changes from 400 to 450
A. 12.5%
B. 50%
C. 11.1%
D. −12.5%

A. 12.5%

RC = (450 − 400)/400 = 50/400 = 0.125 = 12.5%.

Divide by the original, 400.

Textbook Question · Problem 6
Find the relative, or percent, change.
B changes from 12,000 to 15,000
A. 30%
B. 3%
C. 25%
D. 20%

C. 25%

RC = (15,000 − 12,000)/12,000 = 3,000/12,000 = 0.25 = 25%.

Divide by 12,000.

Textbook Question · Problem 7
Find the relative, or percent, change.
R changes from 50 to 47
A. 6%
B. −3%
C. −6.38%
D. −6%

D. −6%

RC = (47 − 50)/50 = −3/50 = −0.06 = −6%.

Divide by 50; the value went down.

Textbook Question · Problem 8
Find the relative, or percent, change.
W changes from 0.3 to 0.05
A. ≈ −500%
B. ≈ −83.3%
C. ≈ −25%
D. ≈ 83.3%

B. ≈ −83.3%

RC = (0.05 − 0.3)/0.3 = −0.25/0.3 ≈ −0.833 = −83.3%.

Divide by 0.3, the original value.

Textbook Question · Problem 42
In Problems 42–45, which relative change is bigger in magnitude? Justify your answer.
The change in the Dow Jones average from 164.6 to 77.9 in 1931; the change from 13261.8 to 8776.4 in 2008.
A. 1931 (≈ −52.7%) is bigger than 2008 (≈ −33.8%)
B. 2008, because 4485.4 points is a bigger drop
C. They are equal
D. 2008 (≈ −33.8%) is bigger than 1931 (≈ −52.7%)

A. 1931 (≈ −52.7%) is bigger than 2008 (≈ −33.8%)

1931: (77.9 − 164.6)/164.6 ≈ −52.7%. 2008: (8776.4 − 13261.8)/13261.8 ≈ −33.8%. The 1931 change is bigger in magnitude.

Compare percentages, not points.

Textbook Question · Problem 43
Which relative change is bigger in magnitude?
The change in the US population from 5.2 million to 7.2 million from 1800 to 1810; the change from 151.3 to 179.3 (million) from 1950 to 1960.
A. 1950–1960 (≈ 38.5%) is bigger
B. They are equal
C. 1950–1960 (≈ 18.5%) is bigger, because 28 million is more than 2 million
D. 1800–1810 (≈ 38.5%) is bigger

D. 1800–1810 (≈ 38.5%) is bigger

1800–1810: 2/5.2 ≈ 38.5%. 1950–1960: 28/151.3 ≈ 18.5%. The 1800–1810 change is bigger.

Relative = compared to the start.

Textbook Question · Problem 44
Which relative change is bigger in magnitude?
An increase in class size from 5 to 10; an increase in class size from 30 to 50.
A. 30 to 50, because 20 students is more than 5
B. 5 to 10 (100% vs 66.7%)
C. 30 to 50 (66.7% vs 100%)
D. They are equal

B. 5 to 10 (100% vs 66.7%)

5 → 10: 5/5 = 100%. 30 → 50: 20/30 ≈ 66.7%. The change from 5 to 10 is bigger.

Divide each change by its own starting value.

Textbook Question · Problem 45
Which relative change is bigger in magnitude?
An increase in sales from $100,000 to $500,000; an increase in sales from $20,000,000 to $20,500,000.
A. They are equal, both increased by $400,000–$500,000
B. $20,000,000 to $20,500,000 (2.5% vs 400%)
C. $100,000 to $500,000 (400% vs 2.5%)
D. $20,000,000 to $20,500,000, because it is larger in dollars

C. $100,000 to $500,000 (400% vs 2.5%)

$100,000 → $500,000: 400,000/100,000 = 400%. $20,000,000 → $20,500,000: 500,000/20,000,000 = 2.5%.

Relative, not absolute.

Find the relative change of a population if it changes
a. From 1000 to 2000
A. 200%
B. 1000%
C. 50%
D. 100%

D. 100%

RC = 1000/1000 = 1 = 100%.

Doubled = +100%.

b. From 2000 to 1000
A. −50%
B. −100%
C. −200%
D. 50%

A. −50%

RC = −1000/2000 = −0.5 = −50%.

Halved = −50%.

c. From 1,000,000 to 1,001,000
A. 10%
B. 0.1%
C. 1%
D. 0.01%

B. 0.1%

RC = 1000/1,000,000 = 0.001 = 0.1%.

A small change compared with a large start.

Textbook Question · Problem 47
On Black Monday, October 28, 1929, the stock market on Wall Street crashed. The Dow Jones average dropped from 298.94 to 260.64 in one day.
What was the relative change in the index?
A. ≈ −14.7%

C. ≈ −12.8%

RC = (260.64 − 298.94)/298.94 = −38.3/298.94 ≈ −0.128 = −12.8%.

Divide by 298.94.

C. ≈ 4.76%

C. ≈ 4.76%

Divide by the original 42 cents.

4. Increasing, Decreasing & Concavity

3 lecture · 11 textbook questions

Lecture Question · Ex 7
Using the given figure, estimate the intervals over which:
(a) The function is increasing; decreasing.
A. Increasing: x < 2 and x > 6; decreasing: 2 < x < 6
B. Increasing: x < 4; decreasing: x > 4
C. Increasing: 2 < x < 6; decreasing: x < 2 and x > 6
D. Increasing: x > 0; decreasing: x < 0

A. Increasing: x < 2 and x > 6; decreasing: 2 < x < 6

The graph rises up to x = 2, falls from x = 2 to x = 6, then rises again after x = 6.

Read from left to right: up, down, up.

(b) The graph is concave up; concave down.
A. Concave up: 2 < x < 6; concave down elsewhere
B. Concave up: x < 4; concave down: x > 4
C. Concave down: x < 4; concave up: x > 4
D. Concave down: x < 2; concave up: x > 6

C. Concave down: x < 4; concave up: x > 4

The graph bends downward (∩) until about x = 4, then bends upward (∪) after x = 4.

∩ = concave down; ∪ = concave up.

Lecture Question · Ex 8
Same as Textbook Problem 10
For which pairs of consecutive points in the given figure is the function:
i. Increasing and concave up?
A. C–D and G–H
B. B–C and F–G
C. D–E and H–I
D. A–B and E–F

C. D–E and H–I

D–E and H–I: going up while bending upward.

Up + ∪.

ii. Increasing and concave down?
A. A–B and E–F
B. B–C and F–G
C. C–D and G–H
D. D–E and H–I

A. A–B and E–F

A–B and E–F: going up while bending downward.

Up + ∩.

iii. Decreasing and concave up?
A. D–E and H–I
B. A–B and E–F
C. B–C and F–G
D. C–D and G–H

D. C–D and G–H

C–D and G–H: going down while bending upward.

Down + ∪.

iv. Decreasing and concave down?
A. C–D and G–H
B. B–C and F–G
C. A–B and E–F
D. D–E and H–I

B. B–C and F–G

B–C and F–G: going down while bending downward.

Down + ∩.

Lecture Question · Ex 9
Use the following values of f(t).
t051015202530
f(t)12.613.114.116.220.029.642.7
(i) Does f appear to be increasing or decreasing?
A. Constant
B. Decreasing
C. Increasing then decreasing
D. Increasing

D. Increasing

f(t) increases from 12.6 to 42.7 as t goes from 0 to 30, so f is increasing.

The values keep getting bigger.

(ii) Do you think its graph is concave up or concave down?
A. Concave up
B. Neither (linear)
C. Concave down, then concave up
D. Concave down

A. Concave up

The ARC between consecutive points is 0.1, 0.2, 0.42, 0.76, 1.92, 2.62: the rate of change is increasing, so the graph is concave up.

Growing faster and faster = concave up.

Table 1.10 gives values of a function w = f(t).
t04812162024

w decreases from 100 to 17. The decreases get smaller (−42, −26, −8, −4, −2, −1), so the rate of change is increasing (less negative): concave up.

Textbook Question · Problem 11
Graph a function f(x) which is increasing everywhere and concave up for negative x and concave down for positive x.
Which description matches such a graph?
A. Always falling; bends upward left of x = 0
B. Always rising; bends downward (∩) left of x = 0 and upward (∪) right of x = 0
C. Rising for x < 0 and falling for x > 0
D. Always rising; bends upward (∪) left of x = 0 and downward (∩) right of x = 0

D. Always rising; bends upward (∪) left of x = 0 and downward (∩) right of x = 0

Increasing everywhere means it always rises. Concave up for x < 0 (∪) and concave down for x > 0 (∩): an S-shaped rising curve.

Like a stretched "S" going up.

Textbook Question · Problem 26
Figure 1.37 shows the length, L, in cm, of a sturgeon (a type of fish) as a function of the time, t, in years.
a. Is the function increasing or decreasing? Is the graph concave up or concave down?
A. Increasing, concave up
B. Increasing, concave down
C. Decreasing, concave down
D. Decreasing, concave up

B. Increasing, concave down

The length increases, but more and more slowly: increasing and concave down.

Rising and flattening = concave down.

b. Estimate the average rate of growth of the sturgeon between t = 5 and t = 15. Give units and interpret your answer in terms of the sturgeon.

B. ≈ 12 cm/year: the sturgeon grows about 12 cm per year
C. ≈ 60 cm/year: the sturgeon grows about 60 cm per year
D. ≈ 0.6 cm/year: the sturgeon grows about 0.6 cm per year

A. ≈ 6 cm/year: the sturgeon grows about 6 cm per year

L(5) ≈ 65 cm and L(15) ≈ 125 cm: ARC ≈ (125 − 65)/10 ≈ 6 cm/year.

Divide the growth by 10 years.

t102030405060
F(t)152228333740
G(t)151821242730

A. F: linear; G: concave down; H: concave up
B. F: concave down; G: concave up; H: linear
C. F: concave up; G: linear; H: concave down
D. F: concave down; G: linear; H: concave up

D. F: concave down; G: linear; H: concave up

F increases by 7, 6, 5, 4, 3 (decreasing rate) → concave down. G increases by 3 each time → linear. H increases by 2, 3, 4, 5, 6 (increasing rate) → concave up.

Textbook Question · Problem 39
Experiments suggest that the male maximum heart rate decreases by 9 beats per minute during the first 21 years of his life, and by 26 beats per minute during the first 33 years.
If you model the maximum heart rate as a function of age, should you use a function that is increasing or decreasing, concave up or concave down?
A. Increasing, concave up
B. Decreasing, concave up
C. Decreasing, concave down
D. Increasing, concave down

C. Decreasing, concave down

The heart rate decreases. The rate of decrease grows: 9/21 ≈ 0.43 then 26/33 ≈ 0.79 beats/min per year, so it falls faster and faster → concave down.

Falling faster and faster = concave down.

Textbook Question · Problem 40
A car starts slowly and then speeds up. Eventually the car slows down and stops.
Graph the distance that the car has traveled against time. Which description matches the graph?
A. Increasing: concave down at first, then concave up
B. Decreasing: concave up, then concave down
C. A straight increasing line
D. Increasing: concave up at first, then concave down, then flat

D. Increasing: concave up at first, then concave down, then flat

Speeding up → distance rises faster (concave up ∪). Slowing down → rises more slowly (concave down ∩). Stopped → flat.

Speeding up = ∪; slowing down = ∩.

5. Average Velocity

1 lecture · 5 textbook questions

Lecture Question · Ex 10
A grapefruit is thrown up in the air. The height of the grapefruit above the ground first increases and then decreases. Height, y, of the grapefruit above the ground t seconds after it is thrown:
t (sec)0123456
y (feet)69014216215010630
Find the average velocity of the grapefruit over the interval t = 4 to t = 6. Explain the sign of your answer.
A. 60 ft/sec; positive because the grapefruit is rising
B. −44 ft/sec; negative because the grapefruit is falling
C. −60 ft/sec; negative because the grapefruit is falling
D. −120 ft/sec; negative because the grapefruit is falling

C. −60 ft/sec; negative because the grapefruit is falling

Average velocity = (30 − 150)/(6 − 4) = −120/2 = −60 ft/sec. It is negative because the height is decreasing (the grapefruit is falling).

Average velocity = change in distance ÷ change in time.

Textbook Question · Problem 21

What is the particle's average velocity from t = 0 to t = 3?

B. 1 m/sec

B. 1 m/sec

v = (s(3) − s(0))/(3 − 0) = (4 − 1)/3 = 1 m/sec.

What is the particle's average velocity from t = 1 to t = 3?

C. 4 m/sec

A. 2 m/sec

v = (s(3) − s(1))/(3 − 1) = (6 − 2)/2 = 2 m/sec.

Textbook Question · Problem 37
In an experiment, a lizard is encouraged to run as fast as possible. Figure 1.39 shows the distance run in meters as a function of the time in seconds.
a. If the lizard were running faster and faster, what would be the concavity of the graph? Does this match what you see?

B. Concave up; no, the graph is nearly a straight line
C. Concave down; yes, the graph bends downward

B. Concave up; no, the graph is nearly a straight line

Running faster and faster → distance grows faster → concave up. The graph is nearly a straight line, so it does not match.

Faster and faster = ∪.

b. Estimate the average velocity of the lizard during this 0.8 second experiment.

Textbook Question · Problem 41
Figure 1.40 shows the position of an object at time t.
a. Draw a line on the graph whose slope represents the average velocity between t = 2 and t = 8. Which line is it?

D. The secant line joining the points on the graph at t = 2 and t = 8

Lecture 4Exponential Functions (1.5)

6 lecture · 31 textbook · 1 past exam questions

1. Growth Factor & Exponential Growth2. Exponential Decay3. Linear vs. Exponential Functions4. Finding Exponential Formulas from Data
📖 شرح المحاضرة — Exponential Functions (1.5)

الشرح فيه 4 أجزاء، بنفس ترتيب الأسئلة تحت. اقري الجزء، وبعدين حلي أسئلته. الفكرة كلها: الكمية تنضرب بنفس الرقم كل سنة (أو كل ساعة).

1️⃣ معامل النمو والنمو الأسي (Growth Factor & Exponential Growth)

الدالة الأسية (Exponential function) شكلها:

P = P0 at
  • P0 = الكمية بالبداية (Initial value)، يعني لما t = 0. هو الرقم اللي قدام.
  • a = معامل النمو (Growth factor)، يعني الرقم اللي تنضرب فيه الكمية كل وحدة زمن.
  • t = الزمن (Time)، غالباً بالسنين.

تخيلي حصالة: كل سنة اللي فيها ينضرب بـ 1.05. هذا نمو أسي. (لو كل سنة ينزاد عليها 5 دنانير بس، هذا خطي، بنشوفه بالجزء 3.)

🔑 العلاقة بين a ونسبة النمو r (Growth rate):
a = 1 + r    ←    r = a − 1
مثال: a = 1.034 يعني r = 0.034 = 3.4% بالسنة.

كيف أعرف a من جدول؟ اقسمي كل قيمة على اللي قبلها. إذا طلع نفس الرقم تقريباً، هذا هو المعامل (والدالة أسية).

مثال (Ex 1): سكان بوركينا فاسو، أوجدي a

الجدول كل سنتين: 12.853 (2003)، 13.747 (2005)، 14.721 (2007)، 15.757 (2009).

P2 / P0 = 13.747 / 12.853 ≈ 1.0695
P4 / P2 = 14.721 / 13.747 ≈ 1.07   (نفس الرقم تقريباً ✓)

لاحظي: هذا المعامل لـ سنتين، يعني a2 ≈ 1.0695. عشان نطلع معامل سنة وحدة ناخذ الجذر التربيعي:

a = (1.0695)1/2
a ≈ 1.034 ← نمو 3.4% بالسنة
مثال (Ex 2): سكان العالم P = 6.4(1.0126)t، و t سنين من 2004

i. نسبة النمو السنوية؟

a = 1.0126 → r = 1.0126 − 1 = 0.0126
r = 1.26% per year

ii. السكان سنة 2004؟ سنة 2004 هي البداية، يعني t = 0، وأي رقم أُس صفر = 1:

P = 6.4(1.0126)0 = 6.4 × 1
6.4 billion

iii. توقع سنة 2010؟ t = 2010 − 2004 = 6:

P = 6.4(1.0126)6
P ≈ 6.9 billion
💡 قراءة سريعة لأي دالة P0at:
الرقم اللي قدام = البداية. إذا a > 1 ← تزيد 📈. إذا 0 < a < 1 ← تنقص 📉. وأكبر a = أسرع نمو.
2️⃣ التناقص الأسي (Exponential Decay)

إذا الكمية تنقص بنسبة ثابتة، المعامل يصير أصغر من 1:

a = 1 − r

مثلاً تنقص 6% ← يبقى 94% ← a = 0.94.

شكل الرسمة (Graph): تبدأ من P0، وتنزل، والنزول يبطى شوي شوي، وتقرب من الصفر بس ما توصله. والمنحنى «مقعر للأعلى (Concave up)»، يعني منحني مثل الكوب ∪.

مثال (Ex 3 i): جرعة كينين 50 mg، تطلع من الجسم بنسبة 6% بالساعة. أوجدي القانون
A0 = 50
a = 1 − 0.06 = 0.94
A = 50(0.94)t
مثال (Ex 3 ii): كم يبقى بعد 24 ساعة؟
A = 50(0.94)24
A ≈ 11.3 mg
مثال (Ex 3 iii): أي وصف يناسب الرسمة؟

تناقص أسي، فالرسمة:

تبدأ من 50، تنزل، مقعرة للأعلى (concave up)، وتقرب من 0

وتمر بالنقطة (24, 11.3) اللي حسبناها.

مثال (Ex 3 iv): من الرسمة، متى يبقى 5 mg؟

كيف تقرين الرسمة:

  1. روحي للمحور العمودي (A) وحطي إصبعك على 5.
  2. امشي أفقياً لين تلمسين المنحنى.
  3. انزلي عمودياً للمحور الأفقي (t) واقري الرقم.
t ≈ 37 hours

(بالحساب الدقيق تطلع 37.2 ساعة.)

3️⃣ الخطي ضد الأسي (Linear vs. Exponential)

هذا أهم جزء بالامتحان. السؤال يقول لك «بكم» تتغير الكمية، وأنتِ تقررين النوع:

إذا السؤال يقول…النوعالقانون
تزيد بكمية ثابتة (0.4 mg per minute)خطي (Linear)A = A0 + mt
تنقص بكمية ثابتةخطي (Linear)A = A0 − mt
تزيد بنسبة % ثابتةأسي (Exponential)A = A0(1 + r)t
تنقص بنسبة % ثابتةأسي (Exponential)A = A0(1 − r)t
🔑 القاعدة: وحدة (mg، ناس، دينار) ← خطي (نجمع). علامة % ← أسي (نضرب).
والرسمة: الخطي خط مستقيم، والأسي منحنى.
مثال (Ex 4): أدرينالين، البداية 15 mg، و t بالدقايق

(a) تزيد 0.4 mg بالدقيقة ← كمية ثابتة ← خطي، الميل (Slope) m = 0.4:

A = 15 + 0.4t

(b) تنقص 0.4 mg بالدقيقة ← خطي، m = −0.4:

A = 15 − 0.4t

(c) تزيد 3% بالدقيقة ← نسبة ← أسي، a = 1 + 0.03:

A = 15(1.03)t

(d) تنقص 3% بالدقيقة ← أسي، a = 1 − 0.03:

A = 15(0.97)t
مثال (Past Exam 2022 Q2): أدرينالين، البداية 10 mg

(a) تنقص 0.6 mg بالدقيقة ← خطي:

A = 10 − 0.6t

(b) تزيد 10% بالدقيقة ← أسي، a = 1 + 0.10 = 1.1:

A = 10(1.1)t
📋 من جدول: إذا الفرق بين القيم ثابت ← خطي. إذا القسمة (النسبة) ثابتة ← أسي.
4️⃣ إيجاد القانون الأسي من البيانات (Finding Exponential Formulas from Data)

إذا عطوك قيمتين بزمنين مختلفين، وقالوا النمو أسي:

🔑 الخطوات:
① حطي سنة البداية t = 0، فـ P0 = القيمة الأولى.
② احسبي الزمن بين القيمتين (t).
③ عوضي: P = P0at، واقسمي على P0.
④ طلعي a بالجذر: a = (القسمة)1/t.
مثال (Ex 5): الذئاب، 14 سنة 1995، و207 سنة 2012
1995 → t = 0 → P0 = 14
2012 → t = 2012 − 1995 = 17
207 = 14 a17
a17 = 207 / 14 ≈ 14.786
a = (14.786)1/17 ≈ 1.172
P = 14(1.172)t ، r = 0.172 = 17.2%

وإذا ما عطوك قيمة البداية؟ مثلاً عندك f(20) و f(23) بس. الحل: اقسمي القيمتين على بعض، فالـ Q0 ينشطب، والأسس تنطرح (23 − 20 = 3).

مثال (Ex 6): f(20) = 88.2 و f(23) = 91.4

a. أوجدي الأساس (Base) a:

Q0a23 / Q0a20 = 91.4 / 88.2
a3 ≈ 1.0363
a = (1.0363)1/3 ≈ 1.012

b. نسبة النمو:

r = 1.012 − 1 = 0.012 = 1.2%

c. احسبي f(25): أول نطلع Q0 من f(20):

88.2 = Q0(1.012)20
Q0 = 88.2 / (1.012)20 ≈ 69.5
f(25) = 69.5(1.012)25
f(25) ≈ 93.6
⚠️ أخطاء شائعة
  • تنقص 6% ← a = 0.94 مو 0.06.
  • تزيد 3% ← a = 1.03 مو 0.03 ولا 3.
  • إذا الجدول كل سنتين، القسمة تعطيك a2، لازم تاخذين الجذر.
  • t = عدد السنين من البداية، مو السنة نفسها (2010 ← t = 6).
🧠 كيف تعرفين نوع السؤال؟
إذا السؤال فيه…سوي
"percent rate of growth" والقانون معطىr = a − 1
"in 2004" وهي سنة البدايةعوضي t = 0 ← الجواب = الرقم اللي قدام
"by 0.4 mg per minute" (وحدة)خطي: A0 ± mt
"by 3% per minute" (نسبة)أسي: A0(1 ± r)t
جدول وتبين aاقسمي كل قيمة على اللي قبلها
قيمتين بسنتين مختلفتيناقسمي، وبعدين جذر 1/t
"use the graph to estimate when"من المحور العمودي ← للمنحنى ← انزلي للمحور الأفقي

✍️ جربي حلي الأسئلة تحت بزر Solve here، والحسابات بتطلع لك على طول.

1. Growth Factor & Exponential Growth

2 lecture · 6 textbook questions

Lecture Question · Ex 1
Use the table to find a (the growth factor of Burkina Faso's population). Population of Burkina Faso (estimated) 2003–2009:
YearPopulation (millions)
2003P₀ = 12.853
2005P₂ = 13.747
2007P₄ = 14.721
2009P₆ = 15.757
a = ?
A. ≈ 1.34
B. ≈ 1.0695
C. ≈ 0.894
D. ≈ 1.034

D. ≈ 1.034

P₂/P₀ = 13.747/12.853 ≈ 1.0695 and P₄/P₂ = 14.721/13.747 ≈ 1.0695. This is the factor for 2 years, so a = (1.0695)^(1/2) ≈ 1.034 (growth rate 3.4% per year).

The table jumps 2 years at a time: take the square root.

Lecture Question · Ex 2
Same as Textbook Problem 8
World population is approximately P = 6.4(1.0126)ᵗ, with P in billions and t in years since 2004.
i. What is the yearly percent rate of growth of the world population?
A. 101.26% per year
B. 12.6% per year
C. 1.26% per year
D. 0.126% per year

C. 1.26% per year

Growth factor a = 1.0126 = 1 + r → r = 0.0126 = 1.26% per year.

r = a − 1.

ii. What was the world population in 2004?
A. 6.48 billion
B. 6.4 billion
C. 6.9 billion
D. 1.0126 billion

B. 6.4 billion

2004 → t = 0: P = 6.4(1.0126)⁰ = 6.4 billion.

Anything to the power 0 = 1.

iii. What does this model predict for the world population in 2010?
A. ≈ 6.9 billion
B. ≈ 7.2 billion
C. ≈ 6.5 billion
D. ≈ 6.48 billion

A. ≈ 6.9 billion

2010 → t = 6: P = 6.4(1.0126)⁶ ≈ 6.9 billion.

t = 2010 − 2004 = 6.

Textbook Question · Problem 1
The following functions give the populations of four towns with time t in years: (i) P = 600(1.12)ᵗ (ii) P = 1,000(1.03)ᵗ (iii) P = 200(1.08)ᵗ (iv) P = 900(0.90)ᵗ
a. Which town has the largest percent growth rate? What is the percent growth rate?
A. (iv), 90%
B. (ii), 3%
C. (iii), 8%
D. (i), 12%

D. (i), 12%

Growth factors: 1.12, 1.03, 1.08, 0.90. The largest is 1.12 → town (i), r = 12%.

Largest base = fastest growth.

b. Which town has the largest initial population? What is that initial population?
A. (iv), 900
B. (i), 600
C. (ii), 1,000
D. (ii), 1,030

C. (ii), 1,000

The initial population is the number in front (t = 0): the largest is 1,000 → town (ii).

P₀ is the coefficient.

c. Are any of the towns decreasing in size? If so, which one(s)?
A. Yes, (ii) and (iv)
B. Yes, (iv)
C. No, all are increasing
D. Yes, (iii)

B. Yes, (iv)

Only (iv) has a base less than 1 (0.90), so it decreases (10% per year).

Base < 1 = decay.

Textbook Question · Problem 2
Each of the following functions gives the amount of a substance present at time t. In each case, give the amount present initially (at t = 0), state whether the function represents exponential growth or decay, and give the percent growth or decay rate.
(a) A = 100(1.07)ᵗ
A. Initial 100; growth; 7%
B. Initial 107; growth; 7%
C. Initial 100; growth; 1.07%
D. Initial 100; decay; 7%

A. Initial 100; growth; 7%

A₀ = 100; a = 1.07 > 1 → growth; r = 7%.

a − 1 = 0.07.

(b) A = 5.3(1.054)ᵗ
A. Initial 5.3; growth; 5.4%
B. Initial 5.3; growth; 54%
C. Initial 1.054; growth; 5.3%
D. Initial 5.3; decay; 5.4%

A. Initial 5.3; growth; 5.4%

A₀ = 5.3; a = 1.054 → growth; r = 5.4%.

0.054 = 5.4%.

(c) A = 3500(0.93)ᵗ
A. Initial 3500; growth; 7%
B. Initial 3255; decay; 7%
C. Initial 3500; decay; 7%
D. Initial 3500; decay; 93%

C. Initial 3500; decay; 7%

A₀ = 3500; a = 0.93 < 1 → decay; rate = 1 − 0.93 = 7%.

Decay rate = 1 − a.

(d) A = 12(0.88)ᵗ
A. Initial 12; growth; 12%
B. Initial 12; decay; 12%
C. Initial 12; decay; 88%
D. Initial 0.88; decay; 12%

B. Initial 12; decay; 12%

A₀ = 12; a = 0.88 → decay; rate = 1 − 0.88 = 12%.

1 − 0.88 = 0.12.

Textbook Question · Problem 8
Same as Lecture Example 2
World population is approximately P = 6.4(1.0126)ᵗ, with P in billions and t in years since 2004.
a. What is the yearly percent rate of growth of the world population?
A. 101.26% per year
B. 0.126% per year
C. 12.6% per year
D. 1.26% per year

D. 1.26% per year

r = 1.0126 − 1 = 0.0126 = 1.26% per year.

r = a − 1.

b. What was the world population in 2004? What does this model predict for the world population in 2010?
A. 6.48 billion; ≈ 6.9 billion
B. 6.4 billion; ≈ 6.48 billion
C. 6.4 billion; ≈ 6.9 billion
D. 6.4 billion; ≈ 7.2 billion

C. 6.4 billion; ≈ 6.9 billion

t = 0 → 6.4 billion; t = 6 → 6.4(1.0126)⁶ ≈ 6.9 billion.

2004 is t = 0; 2010 is t = 6.

c. Use part (b) to find the average rate of change of the world population between 2004 and 2010.
A. ≈ 0.0126 billion people/year
B. ≈ 0.083 billion people/year
C. ≈ 0.5 billion people/year
D. ≈ 1.26 billion people/year

B. ≈ 0.083 billion people/year

ARC = (6.899 − 6.4)/(2010 − 2004) ≈ 0.499/6 ≈ 0.083 billion people/year.

Change ÷ 6 years.

Textbook Question · Problem 11
The consumer price index (CPI) for a given year is the amount of money in that year that has the same purchasing power as $100 in 1983. At the start of 2009, the CPI was 211.
Write a formula for the CPI as a function of t, years after 2009, assuming that the CPI increases by 2.8% every year.
A. CPI = 211 + 2.8t
B. CPI = 211(0.972)ᵗ
C. CPI = 211(2.8)ᵗ
D. CPI = 211(1.028)ᵗ

D. CPI = 211(1.028)ᵗ

P₀ = 211, a = 1 + 0.028 = 1.028: CPI = 211(1.028)ᵗ.

Increase by a percent → multiply by 1 + r.

Textbook Question · Problem 13
(a) Make a table of values for y = eˣ using x = 0, 1, 2, 3.
A. 1, 2.718, 7.389, 20.086
B. 0, 2.718, 7.389, 20.086
C. 1, 2.718, 5.436, 8.155
D. 1, 0.368, 0.135, 0.050

A. 1, 2.718, 7.389, 20.086

e⁰ = 1, e¹ ≈ 2.718, e² ≈ 7.389, e³ ≈ 20.086.

e⁰ = 1.

(b) Plot the points found in part (a). Does the graph look like an exponential growth or decay function?
A. Growth
B. Decay

A. Growth

The values increase faster and faster: exponential growth.

Getting bigger = growth.

(c) Make a table of values for y = e⁻ˣ using x = 0, 1, 2, 3.
A. 1, −2.718, −7.389, −20.086
B. 1, 2.718, 7.389, 20.086
C. 1, 0.368, 0.135, 0.050
D. 0, 0.368, 0.135, 0.050

C. 1, 0.368, 0.135, 0.050

e⁰ = 1, e⁻¹ ≈ 0.368, e⁻² ≈ 0.135, e⁻³ ≈ 0.050.

e⁻ˣ = 1/eˣ.

(d) Plot the points found in part (c). Does the graph look like an exponential growth or decay function?
A. Growth
B. Decay

B. Decay

The values decrease toward 0: exponential decay.

Getting smaller = decay.

Textbook Question · Problem 14
Graph y = 100e⁻⁰·⁴ˣ.
Describe what you see.
A. Starts at 0 and increases, concave up (exponential growth)
B. Starts at 100 and increases, concave down (exponential growth)
C. Starts at 100 and decreases in a straight line to 0 (linear decay)
D. Starts at 100 and decreases, concave up, getting closer to 0 (exponential decay)

D. Starts at 100 and decreases, concave up, getting closer to 0 (exponential decay)

At x = 0, y = 100. The negative exponent makes it decrease, more and more slowly, approaching the x-axis: exponential decay, concave up.

e to a negative power = decay.

2. Exponential Decay

1 lecture · 4 textbook questions

Lecture Question · Ex 3
Same as Textbook Problem 9
A 50 mg dose of quinine is given to a patient to prevent malaria. Quinine leaves the body at a rate of 6% per hour.
i. Find a formula for the amount, A (in mg), of quinine in the body t hours after the dose is given.
A. A = 50(1.06)ᵗ
B. A = 50(0.94)ᵗ
C. A = 50 − 6t
D. A = 50(0.06)ᵗ

B. A = 50(0.94)ᵗ

A₀ = 50, decay rate r = 6% → a = 1 − 0.06 = 0.94. A = 50(0.94)ᵗ.

Leaves at 6% → 94% remains each hour.

ii. How much quinine is in the body after 24 hours?
A. ≈ 11.3 mg
B. ≈ 1.4 mg
C. ≈ 36 mg
D. ≈ 2.0 mg

A. ≈ 11.3 mg

A = 50(0.94)²⁴ ≈ 11.33 mg.

t = 24.

iii. Graph A as a function of t. Which description matches the graph?
A. Starts at 50, decreasing and concave down
B. Starts at 0, increasing and concave up
C. Starts at 50, decreasing and concave up, approaching 0
D. A straight line from 50 down to 0 at t = 24

C. Starts at 50, decreasing and concave up, approaching 0

Exponential decay: starts at A = 50, decreases, bends upward (concave up), approaches 0, and passes through (24, 11.3).

Decay curves bend upward.

iv. Use the graph to estimate when 5 mg of quinine remains.
A. ≈ 37 hours
B. ≈ 24 hours
C. ≈ 45 hours
D. ≈ 30 hours

A. ≈ 37 hours

From the graph, A = 5 at about t = 37 hours (more exactly 37.2).

Go across from 5 mg to the curve, then down.

Textbook Question · Problem 9
Same as Lecture Example 3
A 50 mg dose of quinine is given to a patient to prevent malaria. Quinine leaves the body at a rate of 6% per hour.
a. Find a formula for the amount, A (in mg), of quinine in the body t hours after the dose is given.
A. A = 50 − 6t
B. A = 50(0.94)ᵗ
C. A = 50(0.06)ᵗ
D. A = 50(1.06)ᵗ

B. A = 50(0.94)ᵗ

a = 1 − 0.06 = 0.94: A = 50(0.94)ᵗ.

94% remains each hour.

b. How much quinine is in the body after 24 hours?
A. ≈ 36 mg
B. ≈ 1.4 mg
C. ≈ 2.0 mg
D. ≈ 11.3 mg

D. ≈ 11.3 mg

A = 50(0.94)²⁴ ≈ 11.3 mg.

t = 24.

c. Graph A as a function of t. Which description matches the graph?
A. A straight line from 50 down to 0 at t = 24
B. Starts at 50, decreasing and concave down
C. Starts at 0, increasing and concave up
D. Starts at 50, decreasing and concave up, approaching 0

D. Starts at 50, decreasing and concave up, approaching 0

Exponential decay from 50, concave up, through (24, 11.3).

Decay curves bend upward.

d. Use the graph to estimate when 5 mg of quinine remains.
A. ≈ 37 hours
B. ≈ 24 hours
C. ≈ 45 hours
D. ≈ 30 hours

A. ≈ 37 hours

A = 5 at about t = 37 hours.

Read across from 5 mg.

Textbook Question · Problem 12
During the 1980s, Costa Rica had the highest deforestation rate in the world, at 2.9% per year. (This is the rate at which land covered by forests is shrinking.)
Assuming the rate continues, what percent of the land in Costa Rica covered by forests in 1980 will be forested in 2015?
A. ≈ 64.3%
B. ≈ 2.8%
C. ≈ 35.7%
D. ≈ −1.5%

C. ≈ 35.7%

a = 1 − 0.029 = 0.971; t = 2015 − 1980 = 35. 0.971³⁵ ≈ 0.357 = 35.7%.

35 years of keeping 97.1%.

Textbook Question · Problem 28
(a) Niki invested $10,000 in the stock market. The investment was a loser, declining in value 10% per year each year for 10 years. How much was the investment worth after 10 years?
A. ≈ $9,000
B. ≈ $3,486.78
C. $0
D. ≈ $1,000

B. ≈ $3,486.78

10,000(0.9)¹⁰ ≈ $3,486.78.

Keep 90% each year for 10 years.

(b) After 10 years, the stock began to gain value at 10% per year. After how long will the investment regain its initial value ($10,000)?
A. 10 years
B. ≈ 11.05 years
C. ≈ 7.0 years
D. ≈ 18.5 years

B. ≈ 11.05 years

3,486.78(1.1)ᵗ = 10,000 → 1.1ᵗ ≈ 2.868 → t = ln 2.868/ln 1.1 ≈ 11.05 years.

Losing 10% then gaining 10% does not cancel out.

Textbook Question · Problem 29
A photocopy machine can reduce copies to 80% of their original size. By copying an already reduced copy, further reductions can be made.
a. If a page is reduced to 80%, what percent enlargement is needed to return it to its original size?
A. 120%
B. 80%
C. 25%
D. 20%

C. 25%

0.8 × (1 + r) = 1 → 1 + r = 1.25 → 25% enlargement.

1/0.8 = 1.25.

b. Estimate the number of times in succession that a page must be copied to make the final copy less than 15% of the size of the original.
A. 9 times
B. 5 times
C. 8 times
D. 15 times

A. 9 times

0.8⁸ ≈ 0.168 (still more than 15%); 0.8⁹ ≈ 0.134 < 0.15. So 9 copies.

Keep multiplying by 0.8.

3. Linear vs. Exponential Functions

1 lecture · 11 textbook · 1 past exam questions

Lecture Question · Ex 4
Similar problem (different numbers): Past Exam 2022 Question 2
The amount of adrenaline in the body can change rapidly. Suppose the initial amount is 15 mg. Find a formula for A, the amount in mg, at a time t minutes later if A is:
(a) Increasing by 0.4 mg per minute.
A. A = 15(1.4)ᵗ
B. A = 15(1.004)ᵗ
C. A = 15 − 0.4t
D. A = 15 + 0.4t

D. A = 15 + 0.4t

Constant increase → linear: m = 0.4 mg/min, b = 15. A = 15 + 0.4t.

Constant amount = linear.

(b) Decreasing by 0.4 mg per minute.
A. A = 15(0.996)ᵗ
B. A = 15(0.6)ᵗ
C. A = 15 − 0.4t
D. A = 15 + 0.4t

C. A = 15 − 0.4t

Constant decrease → linear: m = −0.4. A = 15 − 0.4t.

Constant amount = linear.

(c) Increasing by 3% per minute.
A. A = 15 + 0.03t
B. A = 15(1.03)ᵗ
C. A = 15(0.97)ᵗ
D. A = 15(3)ᵗ

B. A = 15(1.03)ᵗ

Constant percent → exponential growth: a = 1 + 0.03 = 1.03. A = 15(1.03)ᵗ.

Constant percent = exponential.

(d) Decreasing by 3% per minute.
A. A = 15 − 0.03t
B. A = 15(1.03)ᵗ
C. A = 15(0.03)ᵗ
D. A = 15(0.97)ᵗ

D. A = 15(0.97)ᵗ

Exponential decay: a = 1 − 0.03 = 0.97. A = 15(0.97)ᵗ.

1 − 0.03 = 0.97.

Textbook Question · Problem 3
Figure 1.62 shows graphs of several cities' populations against time. Match each of the following descriptions to a graph and write a description to match each of the remaining graphs.
a. The population increased at 5% per year.
A. II
B. I
C. III
D. V

A. II

5% per year → exponential growth, the slower one of the two exponential curves: II.

Exponential = curved upward; 5% is slower than 8%.

b. The population increased at 8% per year.
A. IV
B. I
C. III
D. II

B. I

8% → the faster-growing exponential curve: I.

Steeper curve = larger percent.

c. The population increased by 5000 people per year.
A. III
B. VI
C. V
D. II

A. III

Constant increase → increasing straight line: III.

Constant amount = straight line.

d. The population was stable.
A. III
B. IV
C. V
D. VI

C. V

Stable → horizontal line: V.

No change = flat.

IV Write a description for the remaining graph IV.
A. Increasing by a constant percent
B. Stable population
C. Decreasing by a constant number of people per year
D. Decreasing by a constant percent and leveling off

D. Decreasing by a constant percent and leveling off

IV is a decreasing curve that levels off: decreasing by a constant percent.

Curved decrease = exponential decay.

VI Write a description for the remaining graph VI.
A. Stable population
B. Increasing by a constant number of people per year
C. Decreasing by a constant number of people per year
D. Decreasing by a constant percent and leveling off

C. Decreasing by a constant number of people per year

VI is a decreasing straight line: decreasing by a constant number of people per year.

Straight decrease = linear.

Textbook Question · Problem 4
A town has a population of 1000 people at time t = 0. In each of the following cases, write a formula for the population, P, of the town as a function of year t.
a. The population increases by 50 people a year.
A. P = 1000(1.05)ᵗ
B. P = 50 + 1000t
C. P = 1000(50)ᵗ
D. P = 1000 + 50t

D. P = 1000 + 50t

Constant increase → linear: P = 1000 + 50t.

People per year = linear.

b. The population increases by 5% a year.
A. P = 1000(0.95)ᵗ
B. P = 1000(1.05)ᵗ
C. P = 1000 + 5t
D. P = 1000(1.5)ᵗ

B. P = 1000(1.05)ᵗ

Constant percent → exponential: P = 1000(1.05)ᵗ.

5% = 0.05.

Textbook Question · Problem 5
The gross domestic product, G, of Switzerland was 310 billion dollars in 2007. Give a formula for G (in billions of dollars) t years after 2007 if G increases by
(a) 3% per year
A. G = 310(1.03)ᵗ
B. G = 310(0.97)ᵗ
C. G = 310(1.3)ᵗ
D. G = 310 + 3t

A. G = 310(1.03)ᵗ

G = 310(1.03)ᵗ.

Percent → exponential.

(b) 8 billion dollars per year
A. G = 310(1.08)ᵗ
B. G = 310(8)ᵗ
C. G = 310 + 8t
D. G = 8 + 310t

C. G = 310 + 8t

G = 310 + 8t.

Amount per year → linear.

Textbook Question · Problem 6
A product costs $80 today. How much will the product cost in t days if the price is reduced by
(a) $4 a day
A. P = 80 − 4t
B. P = 80 + 4t
C. P = 80(0.96)ᵗ
D. P = 80(0.95)ᵗ

A. P = 80 − 4t

P = 80 − 4t.

Dollars per day → linear.

(b) 5% a day
A. P = 80 − 5t
B. P = 80(0.95)ᵗ
C. P = 80(1.05)ᵗ
D. P = 80(0.05)ᵗ

B. P = 80(0.95)ᵗ

a = 1 − 0.05 = 0.95: P = 80(0.95)ᵗ.

Percent reduction → multiply by 0.95.

Textbook Question · Problem 7
An air-freshener starts with 30 grams and evaporates. In each of the following cases, write a formula for the quantity, Q grams, of air-freshener remaining t days after the start and sketch a graph of the function. The decrease is:
(a) 2 grams a day
A. Q = 30 + 2t (an increasing straight line)
B. Q = 30(0.88)ᵗ (a decreasing curve)
C. Q = 30(0.98)ᵗ (a decreasing curve)
D. Q = 30 − 2t (a decreasing straight line)

D. Q = 30 − 2t (a decreasing straight line)

Constant decrease → linear: Q = 30 − 2t, a straight line falling from 30 to 0 at t = 15.

Grams per day → straight line.

(b) 12% a day
A. Q = 30(0.12)ᵗ (a decreasing curve)
B. Q = 30(0.88)ᵗ (a decreasing curve)
C. Q = 30(1.12)ᵗ (an increasing curve)
D. Q = 30 − 12t (a decreasing straight line)

B. Q = 30(0.88)ᵗ (a decreasing curve)

a = 1 − 0.12 = 0.88: Q = 30(0.88)ᵗ, an exponential decay curve, concave up, approaching 0.

Percent per day → decay curve.

Textbook Question · Problem 22
Find a formula for the number of zebra mussels in a bay as a function of the number of years since 2003, given that there were 2700 at the start of 2003 and 3186 at the start of 2004.
a. Assume that the number of zebra mussels is growing linearly. Give units for the slope of the line and interpret it in terms of zebra mussels.
A. N = 2700 + 486t; 486 mussels/year: increases by 486 each year
B. N = 3186 + 486t; 486 mussels/year: increases by 486 each year
C. N = 2700 + 18t; 18 mussels/year: increases by 18 each year
D. N = 2700(1.18)ᵗ; 18% per year: increases by 18% each year

A. N = 2700 + 486t; 486 mussels/year: increases by 486 each year

m = (3186 − 2700)/1 = 486 mussels/year: N = 2700 + 486t.

One year apart.

b. Assume that the number of zebra mussels is growing exponentially. What is the percent rate of growth of the zebra mussel population?
A. 15.3%
B. 486%
C. 1.18%
D. 18%

D. 18%

a = 3186/2700 = 1.18 → r = 18% per year.

Divide, then subtract 1.

Textbook Question · Problem 23
Worldwide, wind energy generating capacity, W, was 40,300 megawatts in 2003 and 121,188 megawatts in 2008.
a. Use the values given to write W, in megawatts, as a linear function of t, the number of years since 2003.
A. W = 40,300 + 80,888t
B. W = 121,188 + 16,177.6t
C. W = 40,300 + 16,177.6t
D. W = 40,300(1.246)ᵗ

C. W = 40,300 + 16,177.6t

m = (121,188 − 40,300)/5 = 80,888/5 = 16,177.6 MW/year: W = 40,300 + 16,177.6t.

5 years.

b. Use the values given to write W as an exponential function of t.
A. W = 40,300(1.246)ᵗ
B. W = 40,300(3.007)ᵗ
C. W = 40,300 + 16,177.6t
D. W = 40,300(1.601)ᵗ

A. W = 40,300(1.246)ᵗ

121,188 = 40,300a⁵ → a⁵ ≈ 3.007 → a ≈ 1.246: W = 40,300(1.246)ᵗ.

Fifth root of the ratio.

c. Graph the functions found in parts (a) and (b) on the same axes. Which statement is correct?
A. They meet only at (0, 40,300); the exponential is below the line after that
B. Both pass through (0, 40,300) and (5, 121,188); the exponential is below the line between them
C. They never meet; the exponential is always above the line
D. Both pass through (0, 40,300) and (5, 121,188); the exponential is above the line between them

B. Both pass through (0, 40,300) and (5, 121,188); the exponential is below the line between them

Both functions use the same two given values, so both pass through (0, 40,300) and (5, 121,188). Between them the concave-up exponential curve lies below the straight line.

A concave-up curve sits under its secant line.

4. Finding Exponential Formulas from Data

2 lecture · 10 textbook questions

Lecture Question · Ex 5
Wolves were once common in the western US. By the 1990s, the wolf population in Wyoming had been wiped out by hunters and wolves put on the endangered species list. In 1995, wolves were reintroduced to Wyoming from Canada. Starting with 14 wolves, their number increased to 207 wolves in 2012. Assuming the Wyoming wolf population was growing exponentially, find a function of the form P = P₀aᵗ, where P is the population t years after 1995. What is the annual percent growth rate?
P = ? and r = ?
A. P = 14(1.172)ᵗ; r = 17.2%
B. P = 207(1.172)ᵗ; r = 17.2%
C. P = 14(1.172)ᵗ; r = 1.172%
D. P = 14(14.786)ᵗ; r = 1378.6%

A. P = 14(1.172)ᵗ; r = 17.2%

t = 0: P₀ = 14; t = 17: 207 = 14a¹⁷ → a¹⁷ ≈ 14.786 → a ≈ 1.172. P = 14(1.172)ᵗ, r = 0.172 = 17.2%.

2012 − 1995 = 17.

Lecture Question · Ex 6
Suppose Q = f(t) is an exponential function of t. If f(20) = 88.2 and f(23) = 91.4:
a. Find the base.
A. a ≈ 1.036
B. a ≈ 1.0036
C. a ≈ 1.012
D. a ≈ 1.067

C. a ≈ 1.012

Q₀a²³ / Q₀a²⁰ = 91.4/88.2 → a³ ≈ 1.0363 → a ≈ 1.012.

3 time units apart: cube root.

b. Find the percent growth rate.
A. ≈ 12%
B. ≈ 1.2%
C. ≈ 3.6%
D. ≈ 101.2%

B. ≈ 1.2%

r = a − 1 ≈ 0.012 = 1.2%.

r = a − 1.

c. Evaluate f(25).
A. ≈ 69.5
B. ≈ 95.2
C. ≈ 93.6
D. ≈ 92.5

C. ≈ 93.6

Q₀ = 88.2/(1.012)²⁰ ≈ 69.5. f(25) = 69.5(1.012)²⁵ ≈ 93.6.

Find Q₀ first, or multiply f(23) by a².

Textbook Question · Problem 10
The Hershey Company is the largest US producer of chocolate. In 2008, annual net sales were 5.1 billion dollars and were increasing at a continuous rate of 4.3% per year.
a. Write a formula for annual net sales, S, as a function of time, t, in years since 2008.
A. S = 5.1 + 0.043t
B. S = 5.1e^(0.043t)
C. S = 5.1(1.43)ᵗ
D. S = 5.1e^(4.3t)

B. S = 5.1e^(0.043t)

Continuous rate → S = S₀e^(kt) with k = 0.043: S = 5.1e^(0.043t).

"Continuous" → use e.

b. Estimate annual net sales in 2015.
A. ≈ 6.89 billion dollars
B. ≈ 7.20 billion dollars
C. ≈ 6.64 billion dollars
D. ≈ 5.32 billion dollars

A. ≈ 6.89 billion dollars

t = 7: S = 5.1e^(0.043·7) = 5.1e^0.301 ≈ 6.89 billion dollars.

t = 2015 − 2008.

c. Use a graph or trial and error to estimate the year in which annual net sales are expected to pass 8 billion dollars.
A. 2012
B. 2020
C. 2015
D. 2018

D. 2018

5.1e^(0.043t) = 8 → t = ln(8/5.1)/0.043 ≈ 10.5 → in 2018.

Try t = 10, 11.

For Problems 15–16, find a possible formula for the function represented by the data.
x0123
f(x)4.306.028.4311.80
f(x) = ?
A. f(x) = 6.02(1.4)ˣ
B. f(x) = 4.30(0.714)ˣ
C. f(x) = 4.30 + 1.72x
D. f(x) = 4.30(1.4)ˣ

D. f(x) = 4.30(1.4)ˣ

Ratios: 6.02/4.30 ≈ 8.43/6.02 ≈ 11.80/8.43 ≈ 1.4; f(0) = 4.30 → f(x) = 4.30(1.4)ˣ.

Textbook Question · Problem 16

t0123
g(t)5.504.403.522.82

A. g(t) = 5.50(1.25)ᵗ
B. g(t) = 5.50 − 1.1t
C. g(t) = 5.50(0.8)ᵗ
D. g(t) = 5.50(0.2)ᵗ

Ratios: 4.40/5.50 = 3.52/4.40 ≈ 0.8; g(0) = 5.50 → g(t) = 5.50(0.8)ᵗ.

Constant ratio below 1 → decay.

Textbook Question · Problem 17
Give a possible formula for the function in the figure.
y = ?
A. y = 500(1.587)ᵗ
B. y = 500 + 500t
C. y = 500(4)ᵗ
D. y = 2000(1.587)ᵗ

A. y = 500(1.587)ᵗ

y = 500aᵗ; 2000 = 500a³ → a³ = 4 → a = 4^(1/3) ≈ 1.587: y = 500(1.587)ᵗ.

Textbook Question · Problem 18
Give a possible formula for the function in the figure.
y = ?
A. y = 30 − 0.96t
B. y = 30(0.938)ᵗ
C. y = 30(0.2)ᵗ
D. y = 6(0.938)ᵗ

B. y = 30(0.938)ᵗ

y = 30aᵗ; 6 = 30a²⁵ → a²⁵ = 0.2 → a = 0.2^(1/25) ≈ 0.938: y = 30(0.938)ᵗ.

Textbook Question · Problem 19
If the world's population increased exponentially from 4.453 billion in 1980 to 5.937 billion in 1998 and continued to increase at the same percentage rate between 1998 and 2008,
Calculate what the world's population would have been in 2008. How does this compare to the actual population of 6.771 billion?
A. ≈ 6.76 billion, lower than the actual 6.771 billion
B. ≈ 6.37 billion, lower than the actual 6.771 billion
C. ≈ 7.42 billion, higher than the actual 6.771 billion
D. ≈ 6.97 billion, higher than the actual 6.771 billion

D. ≈ 6.97 billion, higher than the actual 6.771 billion

a¹⁸ = 5.937/4.453 → a ≈ 1.0161. 2008: 5.937(1.0161)¹⁰ ≈ 6.97 billion, higher than the actual 6.771 billion.

Find the yearly factor over 18 years, then grow 10 more years.

Textbook Question · Problem 20
The number of passengers using a railway fell from 190,205 to 174,989 during a 5-year period.
Find the annual percentage decrease over this period.
A. ≈ 8.0% per year
B. ≈ 1.65% per year
C. ≈ 0.92% per year
D. ≈ 3.2% per year

B. ≈ 1.65% per year

a⁵ = 174,989/190,205 ≈ 0.920 → a ≈ 0.9835 → decrease ≈ 1.65% per year.

Fifth root of the ratio.

Textbook Question · Problem 21
The company that produces Cliffs Notes (abridged versions of classic literature) was started in 1958 with $4000 and sold in 1998 for $14,000,000.
Find the annual percent increase in the value of this company over the 40 years.
A. ≈ 350% per year
B. ≈ 87.5% per year
C. ≈ 22.6% per year
D. ≈ 2.26% per year

C. ≈ 22.6% per year

a⁴⁰ = 14,000,000/4000 = 3500 → a = 3500^(1/40) ≈ 1.226 → ≈ 22.6% per year.

40th root of 3500.

Textbook Question · Problem 30
Whooping cough was thought to have been almost wiped out by vaccinations. It is now known that the vaccination wears off, leading to an increase in the number of cases, w, from 1248 in 1981 to 18,957 in 2004.
a. With t in years since 1980, find an exponential function that fits this data.
A. w = 1109(1.126)ᵗ
B. w = 1248(15.19)ᵗ
C. w = 1109(1.161)ᵗ
D. w = 1248(1.126)ᵗ

A. w = 1109(1.126)ᵗ

1981 → t = 1, 2004 → t = 24. a²³ = 18,957/1248 ≈ 15.19 → a ≈ 1.126. w₀ = 1248/1.126 ≈ 1109: w = 1109(1.126)ᵗ.

t = 1 in 1981, so w₀ is not 1248.

b. What does your answer to part (a) give as the average annual percent growth rate of the number of cases?
A. ≈ 12.6%
B. ≈ 112.6%
C. ≈ 15.2%
D. ≈ 1.26%

A. ≈ 12.6%

a − 1 ≈ 0.126 = 12.6% per year.

r = a − 1.

c. On May 4, 2005, the Arizona Daily Star reported (correctly) that the number of cases had more than doubled between 2000 and 2004. Does your model confirm this report? Explain.
A. Yes: the model gives exactly double
B. Yes: the model gives about a 126% increase
C. No: the model gives only about a 61% increase
D. No: the model gives a decrease

C. No: the model gives only about a 61% increase

Over 4 years the model multiplies by 1.126⁴ ≈ 1.61, only about a 61% increase, not a doubling.

Compute a⁴.

Textbook Question · Problem 31
Aircraft require longer takeoff distances, called takeoff rolls, at high altitude airports because of diminished air density. The table shows how the takeoff roll for a certain light airplane depends on the airport elevation. (Takeoff rolls are also strongly influenced by air temperature; the data shown assume a temperature of 0° C.)
Elevation (ft)Sea level1000200030004000
Takeoff roll (ft)670734805882967
Determine a formula for this particular aircraft that gives the takeoff roll as an exponential function of airport elevation.
A. R = 670(1.096)^h
B. R = 670(1.096)^(h/1000)
C. R = 670(1.96)^(h/1000)
D. R = 670 + 74h

B. R = 670(1.096)^(h/1000)

Each 1000 ft multiplies the roll by about 1.096 (734/670 ≈ 805/734 ≈ … ≈ 1.096). With h in feet: R = 670(1.096)^(h/1000).

The factor applies per 1000 ft.

Lecture 5The Natural Logarithm (1.6)

6 lecture · 41 textbook questions

No past exam questions for this lecture.

1. The Natural Logarithm & Solving Equations2. Exponential Functions with Base e3. Continuous Growth & Decay Models
📖 شرح المحاضرة — The Natural Logarithm (1.6)

الشرح فيه 3 أجزاء، بنفس ترتيب الأسئلة تحت. اقري الجزء، وبعدين حلي أسئلته. الفكرة كلها: الـ ln ينزّل الأُس (t) من فوق عشان نقدر نحله.

1️⃣ اللوغاريتم الطبيعي وحل المعادلات (The Natural Logarithm & Solving Equations)

المشكلة: بالمعادلة 3t = 10 الـ t فوق بالأُس (Exponent)، وما نقدر نطلعه بالقسمة العادية.

الحل: «اللوغاريتم الطبيعي (Natural logarithm)» واختصاره ln. هو زر بالآلة الحاسبة. تخيليه مثل «مصعد» ينزّل الأُس من فوق لتحت.

e = رقم ثابت مثل π، قيمته تقريباً 2.718.

القاعدةبالرموز
⭐ الـ ln ينزّل الأُس قدامln(at) = t · ln a
⭐ ln و e يلغون بعضln(ex) = x
ln للواحد = صفرln 1 = 0
ln لـ e = واحدln e = 1
ln للسالب أو الصفرما ينفع (Undefined)
🔑 خطوات حل أي معادلة أسية:
① خلّي الأُس بروحه (اقسمي على الرقم اللي قدام).
② خذي ln للطرفين.
③ نزّلي الأُس قدام، وطلعي t بالقسمة.
مثال (Ex 1): أوجدي t إذا 3t = 10

الأُس بروحه أصلاً، فنبدأ بالـ ln على طول:

ln(3t) = ln 10
t · ln 3 = ln 10
t = ln 10 / ln 3
t ≈ 2.096
مثال (Ex 2): أوجدي t إذا 12 = 5e3t

① نخلي الأُس بروحه، نقسم على 5:

12 / 5 = e3t → 2.4 = e3t

② ناخذ ln، والـ ln يلغي الـ e:

ln 2.4 = 3t

③ نقسم على 3:

t = ln 2.4 / 3
t ≈ 0.2918
مثال (Ex 3): سكان نيفادا P = 2.020(1.036)t، متى يوصلون 4 مليون؟

نعوض P = 4 ونحل:

4 = 2.020(1.036)t
1.036t = 4 / 2.020 ≈ 1.980
t · ln 1.036 = ln 1.980
t = ln 1.980 / ln 1.036
t ≈ 19.32 years ← يعني خلال سنة 2019

لاحظي: t سنين من 2000، فـ 2000 + 19.32 = خلال 2019.

2️⃣ الدوال الأسية بأساس e (Exponential Functions with Base e)

فيه طريقتين نكتب فيهم نفس الدالة الأسية:

الصيغةمعنى الرقم
بأساس aP = P0ata = معامل النمو، والنسبة السنوية r = a − 1
بأساس eP = P0ektk = معدل النمو المستمر (Continuous growth rate)

الاثنين متساويين إذا at = ekt، يعني:

a = ek    و    k = ln a
🔑 للتحويل:
من e إلى a ← اضغطي ek بالآلة.
من a إلى e ← اضغطي ln a بالآلة.
والرقم اللي قدام (P0) ما يتغير.
مثال (Ex 4 i): حولي P = 1000e0.05t لصيغة P0at
a = ek = e0.05 ≈ 1.0513
P = 1000(1.051)t
مثال (Ex 4 ii): حولي P = 500(1.06)t لصيغة P0ekt
k = ln a = ln 1.06 ≈ 0.0583
P = 500e0.0583t
💡 مستمر ولا سنوي؟ إذا القانون فيه e ← النسبة مستمرة (continuous) = k. إذا ما فيه e ← النسبة سنوية (annual) = a − 1.
مثال: 1000e0.05t مستمرة 5%، بس سنوياً تطلع 5.13%.
3️⃣ نماذج النمو والتناقص المستمر (Continuous Growth & Decay Models)
P = P0 ekt
  • إذا k موجب ← الكمية تزيد (Growth) 📈
  • إذا k سالب ← الكمية تنقص (Decay) 📉
  • كل ما كان k أكبر ← النمو أسرع.
  • P0 = الكمية الحين (لما t = 0)، لأن e0 = 1.
مثال (Ex 5 i): ارسمي P = e0.5t، نمو مستمر 50%

كيف ترسمين أي دالة أسية: ① عوضي t = 0 عشان تعرفين وين تبدأ. ② شوفي إشارة k: موجب يطلع، سالب ينزل.

t = 0 → P = e0 = 1
k = 0.5 > 0 → growth
تبدأ من 1، تطلع، ومقعرة للأعلى (Concave up)

يعني منحنى يطلع وكل ما مشى يصير أشد، مثل الكوب ∪.

مثال (Ex 5 ii): ارسمي Q = 5e−0.2t، تناقص مستمر 20%
t = 0 → Q = 5e0 = 5
k = −0.2 < 0 → decay
تبدأ من 5، تنزل، مقعرة للأعلى، وتقرب من 0
مثال (Ex 6): أربع مدن A, B, C, D

PA = 600e0.08t ، PB = 1000e−0.02t ، PC = 1200e0.03t ، PD = 900e0.12t

a. أي مدينة تنمو أسرع؟ نقارن k (الرقم اللي بالأُس):

0.08 , −0.02 , 0.03 , 0.12 → الأكبر 0.12
D (12%)

b. أي مدينة أكبر الحين؟ نقارن الرقم اللي قدام (P0):

600 , 1000 , 1200 , 900 → الأكبر 1200
C (1200)

c. فيه مدينة تنقص؟ ندور على k سالب:

Yes, B ← لأن k = −0.02 < 0
⚠️ أخطاء شائعة
  • لا تاخذين ln قبل ما تقسمين: بـ 12 = 5e3t اقسمي على 5 أول.
  • ln 10 / ln 3 مو نفس ln(10/3). اضغطي كل ln بروحه.
  • «أسرع نمو» = أكبر k، و«أكبر الحين» = أكبر رقم قدام. لا تخلطين بينهم.
🧠 كيف تعرفين نوع السؤال؟
إذا السؤال فيه…سوي
"find t" أو "when" أو "after how many years"خلي الأُس بروحه ← ln للطرفين
"to the form P0at" والقانون فيه ea = ek
"to the form P0ekt" والقانون فيه ak = ln a
"sketch the graph"عوضي t = 0 + شوفي إشارة k
"growing fastest"أكبر k
"largest now"أكبر P0
"decreasing"k سالب (أو a < 1)

✍️ جربي حلي الأسئلة تحت بزر Solve here، والحسابات بتطلع لك على طول.

1. The Natural Logarithm & Solving Equations

3 lecture · 16 textbook questions

Lecture Question · Ex 1
Find t such that 3ᵗ = 10.
t = ?
A. t = ln 10 / ln 3 ≈ 2.096
B. t = 10/3 ≈ 3.333
C. t = ln 3 / ln 10 ≈ 0.477
D. t = ln(10/3) ≈ 1.204

A. t = ln 10 / ln 3 ≈ 2.096

ln(3ᵗ) = ln 10 → t ln 3 = ln 10 → t = ln 10 / ln 3 ≈ 2.096.

Take ln of both sides; bring the power down.

Lecture Question · Ex 2
Find t such that 12 = 5e3t.
t = ?
A. t = ln 2.4 ≈ 0.875
B. t = 3 ln 2.4 ≈ 2.626
C. t = ln 12 / 15 ≈ 0.166
D. t = ln 2.4 / 3 ≈ 0.2918

D. t = ln 2.4 / 3 ≈ 0.2918

12/5 = e3t → ln 2.4 = 3t → t = ln 2.4 / 3 ≈ 0.2918.

Divide by 5 first, then take ln.

Lecture Question · Ex 3
If t is in years since 2000, the population of Nevada (in millions) can be modeled by the function P = f(t) = 2.020(1.036)ᵗ.
After how many years will the population of Nevada reach 4 million?
A. t ≈ 55.6 years (during 2055)
B. t ≈ 19.32 years (during 2019)
C. t ≈ 38.9 years (during 2038)
D. t ≈ 1.98 years (during 2001)

B. t ≈ 19.32 years (during 2019)

4 = 2.020(1.036)ᵗ → 1.036ᵗ = 4/2.020 → t = ln(1.980)/ln(1.036) ≈ 19.32 years, so during 2019.

Divide by 2.020, then use ln.

B. t ≈ −0.830

3ᵗ/2ᵗ = 5/7 → (1.5)ᵗ = 5/7 → t = ln(5/7)/ln 1.5 ≈ −0.830.

Isolate the exponential, then take ln of both sides.
