Lecture 6Exponential Growth and Decay (1.7)

8 lecture · 35 textbook · 3 past exam questions

1. Exponential Growth & Decay with Base e2. Doubling Time & Half-Life3. Compound Interest, Present & Future Value
📖 شرح المحاضرة — Exponential Growth and Decay (1.7)

الشرح فيه 3 أجزاء، بنفس ترتيب الأسئلة تحت. اقري الجزء، وبعدين حلي أسئلته.

1️⃣ النمو والتناقص بأساس e (Exponential Growth & Decay with Base e)
P = P0 ekt
  • P0 = الكمية بالبداية، يعني لما t = 0
  • k = معدل النمو المستمر (Continuous growth rate)
  • إذا k موجب ← الكمية تزيد (Growth) 📈
  • إذا k سالب ← الكمية تنقص (Decay) 📉
  • "continuous rate 3%" يعني k = 0.03، و"continuous rate 17% decrease" يعني k = −0.17
🔑 إذا السؤال يقول «متى؟» (when / how long):
① اقسمي على P0 عشان الـ e يصير بروحه ← ② خذي ln للطرفين ← ③ اقسمي على k
مثال (Ex 1 a): إشعاع يود 2.4 millirems/hour، يتناقص بمعدل مستمر k = −0.004. كم الإشعاع بعد 24 ساعة؟
R = 2.4 e−0.004t
R(24) = 2.4 e−0.004×24 = 2.4 e−0.096
R ≈ 2.18 millirems/hour
مثال (Ex 1 b): متى يوصل الإشعاع للحد المسموح 0.6 عشان يرجعون الناس؟
0.6 = 2.4 e−0.004t
0.6 / 2.4 = 0.25 = e−0.004t
ln 0.25 = −0.004t
t = ln 0.25 / (−0.004)
t ≈ 346.6 hours ≈ 14.4 days

لاحظي: ln لرقم أصغر من 1 يطلع سالب، والسالب على السالب يعطي موجب ✓

🔑 إذا عندك قيمتين وتبين k:
① اقسمي القيمة الثانية على الأولى ← ② خذي ln للطرفين ← ③ اقسمي على الزمن
مثال (Ex 2): سكان كينيا 19.5 مليون سنة 1984، و39.0 مليون سنة 2009
1984 → t = 0 → P0 = 19.5
2009 → t = 2009 − 1984 = 25
39.0 = 19.5 e25k
2 = e25k
ln 2 = 25k
k = ln 2 / 25 ≈ 0.0277 ≈ 0.028
P = 19.5 e0.028t   (t years since 1984)

يعني السكان يزيدون بمعدل مستمر تقريباً 2.8% بالسنة.

🔁 تحويل بين الصيغتين:
at = ekt    ←    k = ln a    و    a = ek
مثال: 1.07t = e0.0677t، لأن ln 1.07 = 0.0677
2️⃣ زمن التضاعف وعمر النصف (Doubling Time & Half-Life)
  • «زمن التضاعف (Doubling time)» = الوقت اللي تحتاجه الكمية عشان تصير ضعف (×2).
  • «عمر النصف (Half-life)» = الوقت اللي تحتاجه الكمية عشان تصير نص (×½). مهم وايد بالأدوية 💊
  • الحلو: هالوقت ثابت، ما يعتمد على كمية البداية. سواء بديتي بـ 100 mg أو 1 mg، نفس الوقت.
مثال (Ex 1): أثبتي إن زمن التضاعف لـ Q = Q0at (a > 1) هو t = ln 2 / ln a

تضاعف يعني الكمية صارت 2Q0:

2Q0 = Q0 at
2 = at   (قسمنا على Q0)
ln 2 = t ln a
t = ln 2 / ln a
مثال (Ex 2): تزيد 7% بالسنة، كم زمن التضاعف؟
a = 1 + 0.07 = 1.07
t = ln 2 / ln 1.07 ≈ 10.2 years
مثال (Ex 3): أثبتي إن عمر النصف لـ Q = Q0at (0 < a < 1) هو t = −ln 2 / ln a

عمر النصف يعني الكمية صارت ½Q0:

½Q0 = Q0 at
½ = at
ln ½ = t ln a
−ln 2 = t ln a   (لأن ln ½ = −ln 2)
t = −ln 2 / ln a

الجواب موجب، لأن ln a سالب (a أصغر من 1)، والسالب على السالب = موجب.

صيغة ektصيغة at
زمن التضاعف
الكمية تصير ضعف		T = ln 2 / kT = ln 2 / ln a
عمر النصف
الكمية تصير نص		T = −ln 2 / kT = −ln 2 / ln a
مثال (Ex 4): الأوزون يتناقص بمعدل مستمر 0.25% بالسنة، كم عمر النصف؟

«continuous» ← صيغة e، و«decaying» ← k سالب:

k = −0.25% = −0.0025
T = −ln 2 / k = −ln 2 / (−0.0025) = ln 2 / 0.0025
T ≈ 277 years

والعكس: إذا عطوك عمر النصف وتبين k، اقلبي نفس القانون:

k = −ln 2 / T
مثال (Ex 5) ⭐: البروزاك (Prozac) عمر النصف 3 أيام، كم % يبقى بعد يوم؟ وبعد أسبوع؟
k = −ln 2 / 3 ≈ −0.231 per day

بعد يوم (t = 1): نسبة الباقي = ekt (لأن Q / Q0 = ekt):

e−0.231×1 ≈ 0.79
≈ 79%

بعد أسبوع (t = 7):

e−0.231×7 ≈ 0.20
≈ 20%

نفس الجواب بطريقة ثانية: (½)1/3 ≈ 0.79 و (½)7/3 ≈ 0.20.

💡 قاعدة سريعة: إذا عندك عمر النصف T:
Q = Q0 (½)t/T
وإذا عندك زمن التضاعف T:
Q = Q0 2t/T
🔑 إذا السؤال يقول «تنقص X% خلال كذا ساعة»:
① اللي يبقى = 1 − X% ← ② (الباقي) = ek×الزمن ← ③ طلعي k بالـ ln ← ④ T = −ln 2 / k
مثال (Ex 6) ⭐ مهم: تنقص 4% خلال 10 ساعات، كم عمر النصف؟

تنقص 4% يعني يبقى 96%:

0.96 Q0 = Q0 e10k → 0.96 = e10k
k = ln(0.96) / 10 ≈ −0.00408
T = −ln 2 / k = −ln 2 / (−0.00408)
T ≈ 170 hours

(بالمحاضرة قربوا k إلى −0.004 فطلع ≈ 173 ساعة. الفرق بس من التقريب.)

مثال (Past Exam): تزيد 10% خلال 5 أيام، كم زمن التضاعف؟

تزيد 10% يعني تصير 110%:

1.1 Q0 = Q0 e5k → 1.1 = e5k
k = ln 1.1 / 5 ≈ 0.019
T = ln 2 / k = ln 2 / 0.019
T ≈ 36 days

(بالمحاضرة اعتبروها تقريباً 2% باليوم: ln 2 / ln 1.02 ≈ 35 يوم.)

من جدول: إذا عطوك جدول بقيم، اقسمي كل قيمة على اللي قبلها. إذا طلع نفس الرقم ← هذا a، والقانون Q = Q0at.

مثال (Past Exam 2024 Q4): أمبيسيلين (Ampicillin) 250 mg، والجدول: 250, 150, 90, 54, 32.4, 19.44

a. أوجدي القانون:

150 / 250 = 0.6   و   90 / 150 = 0.6   (ثابت ✓)
Q = 250(0.6)t

b. عمر النصف: صيغة a، و a أصغر من 1:

T = −ln 2 / ln 0.6
T ≈ 1.36 hours

c. متى يوصل 6.9984 mg؟

250(0.6)t = 6.9984
0.6t = 6.9984 / 250 ≈ 0.027994
t = ln(0.027994) / ln 0.6
t = 7 hours
مثال (Past Exam 2022 Q5): أبيكسابان (Apixaban)، يبقى 81.23% بعد 3 ساعات، كم عمر النصف؟

نفس فكرة Ex 6، بس هنا عطونا اللي يبقى على طول:

0.8123 = e3k
k = ln(0.8123) / 3 ≈ −0.0693
T = −ln 2 / k
T ≈ 10 hours
3️⃣ الفائدة المركبة والقيمة الحالية والمستقبلية (Compound Interest, Present & Future Value)

نفس فكرة النمو بالضبط، بس الكمية هنا فلوس 💰.

نوع الفائدةالقانون
سنوية (Annually)B = P(1 + r)t
مستمرة (Continuously)B = P ert
  • P = المبلغ اللي تحطينه الحين، و B = الرصيد (Balance) بعدين
  • r = نسبة الفائدة بصيغة عشرية، يعني 8% تصير 0.08
  • t = عدد السنين
🔮 القيمة المستقبلية (Future value): كم تصير فلوسي بعد t سنة؟ ← B = P ert
⏪ القيمة الحالية (Present value): كم لازم أحط الحين؟ ← P = B e−rt (لاحظي الإشارة السالبة)
مثال (Problem 3): 10,000$ بفائدة 8% مستمرة لمدة 5 سنين
10,000 e0.08×5 = 10,000 e0.4 ≈ $14,918.25
مثال (Problem 4): أبي 20,000$ بعد 6 سنين بفائدة 10% مستمرة، كم أحط الحين؟
20,000 e−0.1×6 = 20,000 e−0.6 ≈ $10,976.23
مثال (Problem 6): 1000$ بفائدة 5.5% لمدة 8 سنين، سنوية ولا مستمرة؟
Annually: 1000(1.055)8 ≈ $1,534.69
Continuously: 1000 e0.055×8 = 1000 e0.44 ≈ $1,552.71

لاحظي: المستمرة تعطي شوي أكثر دايماً.

مثال (Problem 8): 12,000$ بفائدة 8% مستمرة، متى توصل 20,000$؟
20,000 = 12,000 e0.08t
t = ln(20,000 / 12,000) / 0.08 ≈ 6.39 years
⚠️ أخطاء شائعة
  • «تنقص 4%» ← استخدمي 0.96 (اللي يبقى)، مو 0.04.
  • «تزيد 10%» ← استخدمي 1.1، مو 0.1.
  • عمر النصف لازم يطلع موجب. إذا طلع سالب، نسيتي إشارة السالب بالقانون.
  • «continuous» ← صيغة e و k. بدونها ← صيغة a و ln a.
🧠 كيف تعرفين نوع السؤال؟
إذا السؤال فيه…استخدمي
"continuous rate" أو "compounded continuously"ekt
"increases by 7% per year" أو "annually"(1 + r)t
"how long" أو "when"اقسمي وبعدين ln
"doubling time"ln 2 / k  أو  ln 2 / ln a
"half-life"−ln 2 / k  أو  −ln 2 / ln a
"half-life is 3 days" وتبين كم يبقىk = −ln 2 / 3 ← ekt
"decreases by 4% in 10 hours" أو "81.23% remains after 3 hours"الباقي = ek×time ← k ← عمر النصف
قيمتين بزمنين مختلفيناقسميهم على بعض عشان تطلعين k
جدول قيماقسمي كل قيمة على اللي قبلها ← a
"how much now" أو "present value"e−rt

✍️ جربي حلي الأسئلة تحت بزر Solve here، والحسابات بتطلع لك على طول.

1. Exponential Growth & Decay with Base e

2 lecture · 9 textbook questions

Lecture Question · Ex 1
The Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) recently investigated a spill of radioactive iodine. The radiation level at the site was about 2.4 millirems/hour (four times the maximum acceptable limit of 0.6 millirems/hour), so the EPA ordered an evacuation of the surrounding area. The level of radiation from an iodine source decays at a continuous hourly rate of k = −0.004.
(a) What was the level of radiation 24 hours later?
A. ≈ 2.64 millirems/hour
B. ≈ 2.30 millirems/hour
C. ≈ 0.6 millirems/hour
D. ≈ 2.18 millirems/hour

D. ≈ 2.18 millirems/hour

R = 2.4e−0.004t. R(24) = 2.4e−0.096 ≈ 2.18 millirems/hour.

t = 24.

(b) Find the number of hours until the level of radiation reached the maximum acceptable limit, and the inhabitants could return.
A. ≈ 34.7 hours (≈ 1.4 days)
B. ≈ 346.6 hours (≈ 14.4 days)
C. ≈ 173.3 hours (≈ 7.2 days)
D. ≈ 600 hours (25 days)

B. ≈ 346.6 hours (≈ 14.4 days)

0.6 = 2.4e−0.004t → 0.25 = e−0.004t → t = ln 0.25 / (−0.004) ≈ 346.6 hours ≈ 14.4 days.

Divide 0.6 by 2.4 first.

Lecture Question · Ex 2
The population of Kenya was 19.5 million in 1984 and 39.0 million in 2009.
Assuming the population increases exponentially, find a formula for the population of Kenya as a function of time.
A. P = 19.5e0.028t (t years since 1984)
B. P = 19.5e0.04t (t years since 1984)
C. P = 19.5e0.28t (t years since 1984)
D. P = 39.0e0.028t (t years since 1984)

A. P = 19.5e0.028t (t years since 1984)

1984 → t = 0, P₀ = 19.5; 2009 → t = 25, P = 39.0. 39.0 = 19.5e25k → 2 = e25k → k = ln 2/25 ≈ 0.0277 ≈ 0.028. P = 19.5e0.028t.

The population doubled in 25 years.

Textbook Question · Problem 1
World wind energy generating capacity, W, was 18,000 megawatts in 2000 and has been increasing at a continuous rate of approximately 27% per year. Assume this rate continues.
a. Give a formula for W, in megawatts, as a function of time, t, in years since 2000.
A. W = 18,000(1.27)ᵗ
B. W = 18,000 + 0.27t
C. W = 18,000e0.27t
D. W = 18,000e27t

C. W = 18,000e0.27t

Continuous rate → W = 18,000e0.27t.

Continuous → base e.

b. When is wind capacity predicted to pass 250,000 megawatts?
A. t ≈ 5.1 (during 2005)
B. t ≈ 13.9 (during 2013)
C. t ≈ 9.7 (during 2009)
D. t ≈ 51.4 (during 2051)

C. t ≈ 9.7 (during 2009)

250,000 = 18,000e0.27t → t = ln(250/18)/0.27 ≈ 9.7 → during 2009.

Divide, then ln, then ÷ 0.27.

Textbook Question · Problem 14
The exponential function y(x) = Ceαx satisfies the conditions y(0) = 2 and y(1) = 1.
Find the constants C and α. What is y(2)?
A. C = 2, α ≈ 0.693, y(2) = 8
B. C = 2, α ≈ −0.693, y(2) = 0.5
C. C = 2, α = −0.5, y(2) = 0
D. C = 1, α ≈ −0.693, y(2) = 0.25

B. C = 2, α ≈ −0.693, y(2) = 0.5

y(0) = C = 2. 2eα = 1 → α = ln 0.5 ≈ −0.693. y(2) = 2e2α = 2(0.5)² = 0.5.

y(0) gives C directly.

Textbook Question · Problem 15
Air pressure, P, decreases exponentially with the height, h, in meters above sea level: P = P₀e−0.00012h, where P₀ is the air pressure at sea level.
a. At the top of Mount McKinley, height 6194 meters (about 20,320 feet), what is the air pressure, as a percent of the pressure at sea level?
A. ≈ 52.4%
B. ≈ 74.3%
C. ≈ 8.7%
D. ≈ 47.6%

D. ≈ 47.6%

e−0.00012(6194) = e−0.743 ≈ 0.476 = 47.6%.

P/P₀ = e^(−0.00012h).

b. The maximum cruising altitude of an ordinary commercial jet is around 12,000 meters (about 39,000 feet). At that height, what is the air pressure, as a percent of the sea level value?
A. ≈ 23.7%
B. ≈ 14.4%
C. ≈ 47.6%
D. ≈ 76.3%

A. ≈ 23.7%

e−0.00012(12,000) = e−1.44 ≈ 0.237 = 23.7%.

h = 12,000.

Textbook Question · Problem 17
A firm decides to increase output at a constant relative rate from its current level of 20,000 to 30,000 units during the next five years.
Calculate the annual percent rate of increase required to achieve this growth.
A. ≈ 50% per year
B. ≈ 8.45% per year
C. ≈ 10% per year
D. ≈ 8.11% per year

B. ≈ 8.45% per year

20,000a⁵ = 30,000 → a⁵ = 1.5 → a = 1.5^(1/5) ≈ 1.0845 → ≈ 8.45% per year.

Fifth root of 1.5.

Textbook Question · Problem 20
The number of people living with HIV infections increased worldwide approximately exponentially from 2.5 million in 1985 to 37.8 million in 2003. (HIV is the virus that causes AIDS.)
a. Give a formula for the number of HIV infections, H, (in millions) as a function of years, t, since 1985. Use the form H = H₀ekt. Graph this function.
A. H = 37.8e0.151t (increasing, concave up)
B. H = 2.5e−0.151t (decreasing)
C. H = 2.5e0.151t (increasing, concave up)
D. H = 2.5e0.84t (increasing, concave up)

C. H = 2.5e0.151t (increasing, concave up)

37.8 = 2.5e18k → k = ln(15.12)/18 ≈ 0.151 → H = 2.5e0.151t.

2003 − 1985 = 18.

b. What was the yearly continuous percent change in the number of HIV infections between 1985 and 2003?
A. ≈ 15.1% per year
B. ≈ 84% per year
C. ≈ 16.3% per year
D. ≈ 1.51% per year

A. ≈ 15.1% per year

k ≈ 0.151 → ≈ 15.1% per year (continuous).

k is the continuous rate.

Textbook Question · Problem 22
An exponentially growing animal population numbers 500 at time t = 0; two years later, it is 1500.
Find a formula for the size of the population in t years and find the size of the population at t = 5.
A. P = 500(3)ᵗ; P(5) = 121,500
B. P = 500(1.732)ᵗ; P(5) ≈ 4500
C. P = 500(1.5)ᵗ; P(5) ≈ 3797
D. P = 500(1.732)ᵗ; P(5) ≈ 7794

D. P = 500(1.732)ᵗ; P(5) ≈ 7794

500a² = 1500 → a² = 3 → a = √3 ≈ 1.732. P(5) = 500(1.732)⁵ ≈ 7794.

Two years → square root.

Textbook Question · Problem 26
In 1923, koalas were introduced on Kangaroo Island off the coast of Australia. In 1996, the population was 5000. By 2005, the population had grown to 27,000, prompting a debate on how to control their growth and avoid koalas dying of starvation.
Assuming exponential growth, find the (continuous) rate of growth of the koala population between 1996 and 2005. Find a formula for the population as a function of the number of years since 1996, and estimate the population in the year 2020.
A. k ≈ 0.023 (2.3%); P = 5000e0.023t; 2020: ≈ 8,700 koalas
B. k ≈ 0.187 (18.7%); P = 5000e0.187t; 2020: ≈ 449,000 koalas
C. k ≈ 0.54 (54%); P = 5000e0.54t; 2020: ≈ 2.1 billion koalas
D. k ≈ 0.187 (18.7%); P = 5000e0.187t; 2020: ≈ 165,000 koalas

B. k ≈ 0.187 (18.7%); P = 5000e0.187t; 2020: ≈ 449,000 koalas

27,000 = 5000e9k → k = ln 5.4/9 ≈ 0.187. 2020 → t = 24: 5000e0.187(24) ≈ 449,000.

t = 9 for 2005, t = 24 for 2020.

Textbook Question · Problem 27
The total world marine catch in 1950 was 17 million tons and in 2001 was 99 million tons.
If the marine catch is increasing exponentially, find the (continuous) rate of increase. Use it to predict the total world marine catch in the year 2020.
A. k ≈ 0.0345 (3.45%); 2020: ≈ 130 million tons
B. k ≈ 0.0351 (3.51%); 2020: ≈ 198 million tons
C. k ≈ 0.0345 (3.45%); 2020: ≈ 191 million tons
D. k ≈ 1.61 (161%); 2020: ≈ 130 million tons

C. k ≈ 0.0345 (3.45%); 2020: ≈ 191 million tons

99 = 17e51k → k = ln(99/17)/51 ≈ 0.0345. 2020 → t = 70: 17e0.0345(70) ≈ 191 million tons.

t = 70 for 2020.

Textbook Question · Problem 30
In 2004, the world's population was 6.4 billion, and the population was projected to reach 8.5 billion by the year 2030.
What annual growth rate is projected?
A. ≈ 1.3% per year
B. ≈ 0.08% per year
C. ≈ 3.3% per year
D. ≈ 1.1% per year

D. ≈ 1.1% per year

6.4a²⁶ = 8.5 → a = (8.5/6.4)^(1/26) ≈ 1.011 → ≈ 1.1% per year.

26 years.

2. Doubling Time & Half-Life

6 lecture · 15 textbook · 3 past exam questions

Lecture Question · Ex 1 (Doubling Time & Half-Life)
Let Q = Q₀aᵗ, a > 1.
Show that the doubling time for Q is t = ln 2 / ln a. Which derivation is correct?
A. 2Q₀ = Q₀aᵗ → 2 = aᵗ → ln 2 = t ln a → t = ln 2 / ln a
B. 2Q₀ = Q₀aᵗ → 2 = at → t = 2/a
C. Q₀ = 2Q₀aᵗ → 1/2 = aᵗ → t = −ln 2 / ln a
D. 2Q₀ = Q₀ + aᵗ → aᵗ = Q₀ → t = ln Q₀ / ln a

A. 2Q₀ = Q₀aᵗ → 2 = aᵗ → ln 2 = t ln a → t = ln 2 / ln a

Doubling: Q = 2Q₀. 2Q₀ = Q₀aᵗ → 2 = aᵗ → ln 2 = t ln a → t = ln 2 / ln a.

Doubling means Q = 2Q₀.

Lecture Question · Ex 2 (Doubling Time & Half-Life)
Same as Textbook Problem 7
Find the doubling time of a quantity that is increasing by 7% per year.
t = ?
A. ≈ 10.2 years
B. ≈ 7 years
C. ≈ 14.3 years
D. ≈ 9.9 years

A. ≈ 10.2 years

a = 1.07 → t = ln 2 / ln 1.07 ≈ 10.2 years.

t = ln 2 / ln a.

Lecture Question · Ex 3 (Doubling Time & Half-Life)
Let Q = Q₀aᵗ, 0 < a < 1.
Show that the half-life for Q is t = −ln 2 / ln a. Which derivation is correct?
A. ½Q₀ = Q₀ − aᵗ → aᵗ = ½Q₀ → t = ln Q₀ / ln a
B. ½Q₀ = Q₀aᵗ → ½ = aᵗ → ln ½ = t ln a → t = −ln 2 / ln a
C. ½Q₀ = Q₀aᵗ → ½ = at → t = 1/(2a)
D. 2Q₀ = Q₀aᵗ → 2 = aᵗ → t = ln 2 / ln a

B. ½Q₀ = Q₀aᵗ → ½ = aᵗ → ln ½ = t ln a → t = −ln 2 / ln a

Half-life: Q = ½Q₀. ½ = aᵗ → ln(½) = t ln a → −ln 2 = t ln a → t = −ln 2 / ln a (positive, since ln a < 0).

ln(½) = −ln 2.

Lecture Question · Ex 4 (Doubling Time & Half-Life)
The release of chlorofluorocarbons used in air conditioners and household sprays (hair spray, shaving cream, etc.) destroys the ozone in the upper atmosphere. The quantity of ozone, Q, is decaying exponentially at a continuous rate of 0.25% per year.
What is the half-life of ozone? In other words, at this rate, how long will it take for half the ozone to disappear?
A. ≈ 400 years
B. ≈ 2.77 years
C. ≈ 277 years
D. ≈ 200 years

C. ≈ 277 years

k = −0.0025. t = −ln 2 / k = ln 2 / 0.0025 ≈ 277 years.

0.25% = 0.0025.

Lecture Question · Ex 5 (Doubling Time & Half-Life)
Same as Textbook Problem 16
The antidepressant fluoxetine (or Prozac) has a half-life of about 3 days.
What percentage of a dose remains in the body after one day (t = 1)? After one week (t = 7)?
A. After 1 day ≈ 79%; after 1 week ≈ 50%
B. After 1 day ≈ 83%; after 1 week ≈ 29%
C. After 1 day ≈ 67%; after 1 week ≈ 0%
D. After 1 day ≈ 79%; after 1 week ≈ 20%

D. After 1 day ≈ 79%; after 1 week ≈ 20%

k = −ln 2/3 ≈ −0.231 per day. e−0.231 ≈ 0.79 = 79%; e−0.231(7) ≈ 0.20 = 20%.

Find k from the half-life first.

Lecture Question · Ex 6 (Doubling Time & Half-Life)
Same as Textbook Problem 23
If the quantity of a substance decreases by 4% in 10 hours,
find its half-life.
A. ≈ 125 hours
B. ≈ 17 hours
C. ≈ 170 hours
D. ≈ 250 hours

C. ≈ 170 hours

0.96 = e10k → k = ln 0.96/10 ≈ −0.00408 → t = −ln 2/k ≈ 170 hours. (The lecture rounds k to −0.004 and gets ≈ 173 hours.)

96% remains after 10 hours.

Past Exam Question · Past Exam (Lecture)
If the quantity of a substance increases by 10% in 5 days,
find its doubling-time.
A. ≈ 25 days
B. ≈ 36 days
C. ≈ 7.3 days
D. ≈ 50 days

B. ≈ 36 days

1.1Q₀ = Q₀e5k → k = ln 1.1/5 ≈ 0.019 → t = ln 2/0.019 ≈ 36 days. (The lecture uses 2% per day: ln 2/ln 1.02 ≈ 35 days.)

110% after 5 days.

Textbook Question · Problem 2
The half-life of nicotine in the blood is 2 hours. A person absorbs 0.4 mg of nicotine by smoking a cigarette.
t (hours)0246810
Nicotine (mg)0.4?????
Table Fill in the table with the amount of nicotine remaining in the blood after t hours.
A. 0.4, 0.8, 1.6, 3.2, 6.4, 12.8
B. 0.4, 0.3, 0.2, 0.1, 0, 0
C. 0.4, 0.1, 0.025, 0.00625, 0.0016, 0.0004
D. 0.4, 0.2, 0.1, 0.05, 0.025, 0.0125

D. 0.4, 0.2, 0.1, 0.05, 0.025, 0.0125

Every 2 hours the amount halves: 0.4 → 0.2 → 0.1 → 0.05 → 0.025 → 0.0125 mg.

Halve each step.

Time Estimate the length of time until the amount of nicotine is reduced to 0.04 mg.
A. ≈ 6.6 hours
B. ≈ 10 hours
C. ≈ 4 hours
D. ≈ 20 hours

A. ≈ 6.6 hours

0.04 is between 0.05 (t = 6) and 0.025 (t = 8). Exactly: 0.4(0.5)^(t/2) = 0.04 → t = 2 ln 10 / ln 2 ≈ 6.6 hours.

It drops to one tenth.

Textbook Question · Problem 5
If a bank pays 6% per year interest compounded continuously,
how long does it take for the balance in an account to double?
A. ≈ 16.67 years
B. ≈ 8.33 years
C. ≈ 11.55 years
D. ≈ 11.90 years

C. ≈ 11.55 years

t = ln 2 / 0.06 ≈ 11.55 years.

Continuous: t = ln 2 / k.

Textbook Question · Problem 7
Same as Lecture Example 2 (Doubling Time and Half-Life)
Find the doubling time of a quantity that is increasing by 7% per year.
t = ?
A. ≈ 9.90 years
B. 7 years
C. ≈ 14.29 years
D. ≈ 10.24 years

D. ≈ 10.24 years

t = ln 2 / ln 1.07 ≈ 10.24 years.

t = ln 2 / ln a.

Textbook Question · Problem 10
From October 2002 to October 2006 the number N(t) of Wikipedia articles was approximated by N(t) = N₀et/500, where t is the number of days after October 1, 2002.
Find the doubling time for the number of Wikipedia articles during this period.
A. ≈ 346.6 days
B. ≈ 500 days
C. ≈ 250 days
D. ≈ 721 days

A. ≈ 346.6 days

k = 1/500 = 0.002 → t = ln 2/0.002 = 500 ln 2 ≈ 346.6 days.

k = 1/500.

Textbook Question · Problem 11
A cup of coffee contains 100 mg of caffeine, which leaves the body at a continuous rate of 17% per hour.
a. Write a formula for the amount, A mg, of caffeine in the body t hours after drinking a cup of coffee.
A. A = 100e0.17t
B. A = 100e−0.17t
C. A = 100(0.83)ᵗ
D. A = 100 − 17t

B. A = 100e−0.17t

Continuous decay at 17% → A = 100e−0.17t.

Continuous → base e, negative k.

b. Graph the function from part (a). Use the graph to estimate the half-life of caffeine.
A. Straight line from 100; A = 50 at t ≈ 3 hours
B. Increasing curve; A = 200 at about t ≈ 4 hours
C. Decreasing, concave-up curve from 100; A = 50 at about t ≈ 8 hours

Lecture 7New Functions From Old (1.8)

10 lecture · 43 textbook · 1 past exam questions

1. Composite Functions2. Stretches, Shifts & Reflections
📖 شرح المحاضرة — New Functions From Old (1.8)

المحاضرة عن شغلتين: ① نحط دالة داخل دالة (Composite)، و② نحرك الرسمة يمين ويسار وفوق وتحت (Shifts). الشرح فيه 5 أجزاء بنفس ترتيب الأسئلة. اقري الجزء، وبعدين حلي أسئلته.

1️⃣ الدالة المركبة بالقانون (Composite Functions)

تخيلي الدالة مكينة 🏭: تدخلين فيها رقم أو شي، وتطلع لك نتيجة.

  • f(x) = x² يعني: المكينة f تاخذ أي شي وتربعه.
  • الحرف x مجرد مكان فاضي. اللي تحطينه بين القوسين، يروح مكان كل x.
  • مثال: f(5) = 5² = 25، و f(t + 1) = (t + 1)²

الدالة المركبة (Composite function) = دالة داخل دالة:

f(g(x))
  • نبدأ من الداخل: نحسب g(x) أول.
  • بعدين النتيجة ندخلها في f.
  • g = الدالة الداخلية (Inside function)، و f = الدالة الخارجية (Outside function).
🔑 طريقة الحل:
① اكتبي قانون g مكان g(x) ← ② روحي لقانون f وحطي القوس كله مكان كل x ← ③ بسطي
مثال (Ex 1): f(x) = 2x / (3x − 7) و g(x) = x + 1، أوجدي f(g(x))

نحط (x + 1) مكان كل x في f:

f(g(x)) = f(x + 1)
= 2(x + 1) / (3(x + 1) − 7)
= (2x + 2) / (3x + 3 − 7)
= (2x + 2) / (3x − 4)
مثال (Ex 2): f(t) = t² و g(t) = t + 2

هني الحرف t بدال x، نفس الفكرة.

(a) f(t + 1) = (t + 1)²
(b) f(t) + 3 = t² + 3   ← (+3 برا القوس، نضيفها بعد التربيع)
(c) f(t + h) = (t + h)²
(d) f(g(t)) = f(t + 2) = (t + 2)²
(e) g(f(t)) = g(t²) = t² + 2

لاحظي: (d) و (e) طلعوا مختلفين. يعني الترتيب مهم.

مثال (Ex 3): f(x) = eˣ و g(x) = 5x + 1
(a) f(g(x)) = f(5x + 1) = e5x + 1

في (b) الداخلية صارت eˣ، فنحطها مكان x في g:

(b) g(f(x)) = g(eˣ) = 5eˣ + 1
2️⃣ الدالة المركبة من جدول أو رسمة (From a Table / Graph)

نفس القاعدة: نبدأ من الداخل. بس بدال القانون، نطلع القيم من الجدول أو الرسمة.

🔑 من الجدول: لـ g(f(0)): ① دوري x = 0 في صف f ← ② الجواب صار x جديد ← ③ دوريه في صف g
مثال (Ex 4): من الجدول
x0123
f(x)31−1−3
g(x)0246
(a) f(0) = 3 → g(3) = 6
(b) g(0) = 0 → f(0) = 3
(c) f(1) = 1 → g(1) = 2
(d) g(1) = 2 → f(2) = −1
📈 من الرسمة: عشان تقرين g(1): روحي على المحور الأفقي (x-axis) لين x = 1 ← اطلعي لفوق لين توصلين خط g ← شوفي الارتفاع على المحور العمودي (y-axis). هذا هو g(1).
مثال (Ex 5): من الرسمتين، قدري f(g(1))
① من رسمة g: عند x = 1 الارتفاع 2 ← g(1) = 2
② من رسمة f: عند x = 2 الارتفاع 4 ← f(2) = 4
f(g(1)) = 4
3️⃣ نفك الدالة لداخلية وخارجية (Inside & Outside Function)

هني العكس: عندك دالة كبيرة، ونبي نقسمها لـ داخلية u و خارجية.

🔑 الداخلية u = اللي داخل القوس، أو تحت الجذر، أو فوق في الأس (exponent).
بعدين نكتب الدالة نفسها بس نحط u مكان هذا الجزء.
مثال (Ex 6): اكتبيها كدالة مركبة باستخدام u
(a) y = ln(3t) ← داخل الـ ln: u = 3t ، y = ln u
(b) w = 5(2r + 3)² ← داخل القوس: u = 2r + 3 ، w = 5u²
(c) P = e−0.03t ← فوق في الأس: u = −0.03t ، P = eᵘ
4️⃣ الانعكاس والتمدد (Reflections & Stretches)

أول شي نعرف رسمة y = x². اسمها القطع المكافئ (Parabola)، شكلها مثل حرف U.

مثال (Ex 7): ارسمي y = x² و y = −x²

نعوض كم رقم:

x−2−1012
x²41014
−x²−4−10−1−4
(a) y = x² : U مفتوح لفوق، الرأس (vertex) عند (0, 0)
(b) y = −x² : نفس الشكل مقلوب، مفتوح لتحت، الرأس (0, 0)

السالب قلب الرسمة حول محور x. هذا اسمه انعكاس (Reflection)، مثل المراية 🪞.

التغييرشنو يصير بالرسمة
−f(x)انعكاس حول محور x (تنقلب) 🙃
2f(x)تمدد عمودي (Vertical stretch): تطول ×2
⅓ f(x)انكماش عمودي (Vertical compression): تقصر ×⅓
🔑 الضرب برا يغير الطول بس (قيم y). النقاط اللي على محور x (يعني y = 0) ما تتحرك، لأن 0 × أي رقم = 0.
مثال (Ex 8): y = √(9 − x²) وتغييراتها

نعوض: x = −3 → 0 ، x = 0 → √9 = 3 ، x = 3 → 0. الرسمة نص دائرة فوق (Upper semicircle) نصف قطرها 3.

(a) √(9 − x²) : نص دائرة فوق، من (−3, 0) إلى (3, 0)، أعلى نقطة (0, 3)
(b) −√(9 − x²) : انعكاس ← نص دائرة تحت، أوطى نقطة (0, −3)
(c) 2√(9 − x²) : تمدد ×2 ← نفس الأطراف (±3, 0)، أعلى نقطة (0, 6)
(d) (1/3)√(9 − x²) : انكماش ← نفس الأطراف (±3, 0)، أعلى نقطة (0, 1)
5️⃣ الإزاحة (Shifts)
المكانالدالةالحركة
برا (Outside)f(x) + 3فوق 3 ⬆️
براf(x) − 3تحت 3 ⬇️
داخل (Inside)f(x − 2)يمين 2 ➡️
داخلf(x + 2)يسار 2 ⬅️
🔑 برا القوس ← فوق/تحت، نفس الإشارة (+ فوق).
داخل القوس ← يمين/يسار، عكس الإشارة (− يمين، + يسار).

نحتاج نعرف رسمتين أساسيتين:

  • y = eˣ: تمر بـ (0, 1)، وتقرب من y = 0 على اليسار بدون ما تلمسه.
  • y = ln x: تمر بـ (1, 0)، وتقرب من x = 0 بدون ما تلمسه.
  • هالخط اللي تقرب منه الرسمة وما تلمسه اسمه خط مقارب (Asymptote).
مثال (Ex 9): ارسمي eˣ + 2 و ln(x − 2)

(a) +2 برا ← فوق 2. كل نقطة ترتفع 2، والخط المقارب بعد:

(0, 1) → (0, 3)    و    y = 0 → y = 2

(b) −2 داخل ← يمين 2:

(1, 0) → (3, 0)    و    x = 0 → x = 2
مثال (Ex 10): حركي الـ Parabola

الأصل y = x² رأسه (0, 0). نحرك الرأس:

(a) x² + 3 ← برا +3 ← فوق 3 ← الرأس (0, 3)
(b) (x + 3)² ← داخل +3 ← يسار 3 ← الرأس (−3, 0)
(c) (x − 2)² ← داخل −2 ← يمين 2 ← الرأس (2, 0)
مثال (Past Exam 2024): المورفين بدال 8 الصبح يبدا 12 الظهر

f(t) = كمية المورفين بالدم بعد t ساعة من 8 الصبح. لو بدينا 12 الظهر، يعني كل شي يتأخر 4 ساعات.

التأخير = حركة لليمين 4 (على محور الوقت)
a) نفس المنحنى بس متحرك 4 يمين: Q = 0 لين t = 4، بعدين يرتفع ويقرب من 7.2
b) يمين 4 ← داخل القوس −4 ← g(t) = f(t − 4)
🧠 كيف تعرفين نوع السؤال؟
إذا السؤال فيه…سوي
f(g(x))حطي قانون g مكان كل x في f
f(g(1)) مع جدول أو رسمةطلعي g(1) أول، بعدين حطيه في f
"use a new variable u" أو "inside function"u = اللي داخل القوس/الجذر/الأس
سالب قدام الدالة −f(x)اقلبيها حول محور x
رقم مضروب قدام الدالة 2f(x)طوليها أو قصريها (عمودي)
رقم مضاف برا f(x) + kفوق/تحت بنفس الإشارة
رقم داخل القوس f(x − h)يمين/يسار بعكس الإشارة
"starts later" أو "at noon instead of 8 am"يمين ← f(t − 4)
⚠️ أخطاء شائعة:
• f(g(x)) غير g(f(x))، ابدي دايماً من الداخل.
• f(x − 2) يعني يمين مو يسار.
• f(t) + 3 مو نفس f(t + 3): الأولى فوق، والثانية يسار.
• لما تعوضين، حطي قوس كامل: 3(x + 1) مو 3x + 1.

✍️ جربي حلي الأسئلة تحت بزر Solve here، والحسابات بتطلع لك على طول.

1. Composite Functions

6 lecture · 27 textbook questions

Lecture Question · Ex 1
If f(x) = 2x / (3x − 7) and g(x) = x + 1,
find f(g(x)).
A. (2x + 2)/(3x − 4)
B. 2x/(3x − 7) + 1
C. (2x + 2)/(3x − 7)
D. (2x + 1)/(3x − 6)

A. (2x + 2)/(3x − 4)

f(g(x)) = f(x + 1) = 2(x + 1)/(3(x + 1) − 7) = (2x + 2)/(3x − 4).

Replace every x in f by (x + 1).

Lecture Question · Ex 2
If f(t) = t² and g(t) = t + 2, find
(a) f(t + 1)
A. t + 1
B. (t + 1)²
C. (t + 2)²
D. t² + 1

B. (t + 1)²

f(t + 1) = (t + 1)².

Replace t by t + 1 inside f.

(b) f(t) + 3
A. t + 5
B. 3t²
C. t² + 3
D. (t + 3)²

C. t² + 3

f(t) + 3 = t² + 3.

Add 3 outside.

(c) f(t + h)
A. t² + h
B. (t + h)
C. t² + h²
D. (t + h)²

D. (t + h)²

f(t + h) = (t + h)².

Replace t by t + h.

(d) f(g(t))
A. (t + 2)²
B. t² + 4
C. t² + 2
D. t + 4

A. (t + 2)²

f(g(t)) = f(t + 2) = (t + 2)².

Inside function g goes first.

(e) g(f(t))
A. 2t²
B. t + 4
C. (t + 2)²
D. t² + 2

D. t² + 2

g(f(t)) = g(t²) = t² + 2.

Now f goes first.

A. e5x + 1
B. 5ex+1
C. e5x+1
D. 5eˣ + 1

C. e5x+1

f(g(x)) = f(5x + 1) = e5x+1.

g goes in the exponent.

(b) g(f(x))
A. e5x + 1
B. 5eˣ + 1
C. e5x+1
D. 5ex+1

B. 5eˣ + 1

g(f(x)) = g(eˣ) = 5eˣ + 1.

Multiply eˣ by 5, then add 1.

Lecture Question · Ex 6
Use a new variable u for the inside function to express each of the following as a composite function:
(a) y = ln(3t)
A. u = 3t, y = ln u
B. u = 3, y = ln(ut)
C. u = ln t, y = 3u
D. u = ln 3t, y = u

A. u = 3t, y = ln u

Inside function u = 3t; outside y = ln u.

The inside is what ln acts on.

B. u = 2r, w = 5(u + 3)

D. u = 2r + 3, w = 5u²

u = 2r + 3; w = 5u².

The inside is the bracket.

A. u = et, P = −0.03u
B. u = −0.03t, P = eᵘ
C. u = −0.03, P = eut
D. u = e−0.03t, P = u²

B. u = −0.03t, P = eᵘ

u = −0.03t; P = eᵘ.

Textbook Question · Problem 1
For g(x) = x² + 2x + 3, find and simplify:
(a) g(2 + h)
A. h² + 2h + 11
B. h² + 6h + 11
C. h² + 6h + 3
D. 4 + h² + 2h + 3

B. h² + 6h + 11

Expand (2 + h)² carefully.

(b) g(2)
A. 7
B. 9
C. 11
D. 15

C. 11

4 + 4 + 3 = 11.

x = 2.

(c) g(2 + h) − g(2)
A. h² + 6h − 11
B. 6h
C. h² + 6h + 11
D. h² + 6h

D. h² + 6h

Subtract part (b) from part (a).

Textbook Question · Problem 23
A tree of height y meters has, on average, B branches, where B = y − 1. Each branch has, on average, n leaves where n = 2B² − B.
Find the average number of leaves of a tree as a function of height.
A. Leaves = 2(y − 1)² − (y − 1)
B. Leaves = 2(y − 1)³ − (y − 1)²
C. Leaves = 2(y − 1)² − y
D. Leaves = 2y³ − y²

B. Leaves = 2(y − 1)³ − (y − 1)²

Leaves = n · B = (2B² − B)B = 2B³ − B², with B = y − 1: Leaves = 2(y − 1)³ − (y − 1)².

Total leaves = leaves per branch × number of branches.

2. Stretches, Shifts & Reflections

4 lecture · 16 textbook · 1 past exam questions

Lecture Question · Ex 7
Sketch the graph of the functions:
(a) y = x²
A. A parabola opening upward with vertex (0, 1)
B. A straight line through the origin
C. A parabola opening downward with vertex (0, 0)
D. A parabola opening upward with vertex (0, 0)

D. A parabola opening upward with vertex (0, 0)

y = x² is a U-shaped parabola opening upward, vertex at the origin.

x² is never negative.

(b) y = −x²
A. A parabola opening downward with vertex (0, 0)
B. A parabola opening downward with vertex (0, −1)
C. A parabola opening upward with vertex (0, 0)
D. A straight line with slope −1

A. A parabola opening downward with vertex (0, 0)

y = −x² is the reflection of y = x² across the x-axis: opening downward, vertex (0, 0).

The minus sign flips it.

Lecture Question · Ex 8
a) Using Desmos, sketch the graph of y = √(9 − x²).
A. A parabola opening downward with vertex (0, 9)
B. A full circle of radius 9
C. The upper half of a circle of radius 3, from (−3, 0) to (3, 0) with top (0, 3)
D. The lower half of a circle of radius 3

C. The upper half of a circle of radius 3, from (−3, 0) to (3, 0) with top (0, 3)

y = √(9 − x²) ≥ 0 is the upper semicircle of radius 3 centered at the origin.

x² + y² = 9 with y ≥ 0.

b) Sketch the graph of y = −√(9 − x²).
A. The upper half stretched to height 6
B. The lower half of the circle, with bottom (0, −3)
C. The upper half of the circle, with top (0, 3)
D. The upper half shifted down 3

B. The lower half of the circle, with bottom (0, −3)

The minus sign reflects the upper semicircle across the x-axis: the lower semicircle, lowest point (0, −3).

Reflection across the x-axis.

c) Sketch the graph of y = 2√(9 − x²).
A. The upper semicircle shifted up 2: top (0, 5)
B. The upper semicircle compressed: top (0, 1.5)
C. The upper semicircle stretched horizontally: from (−6, 0) to (6, 0) with top (0, 3)
D. The upper semicircle stretched vertically: from (−3, 0) to (3, 0) with top (0, 6)

D. The upper semicircle stretched vertically: from (−3, 0) to (3, 0) with top (0, 6)

Multiplying by 2 stretches vertically by 2: same ends (±3, 0), top at (0, 6).

Outside × 2 = vertical stretch.

d) Sketch the graph of y = (1/3)√(9 − x²).
A. The upper semicircle compressed vertically: from (−3, 0) to (3, 0) with top (0, 1)
B. The upper semicircle compressed horizontally: from (−1, 0) to (1, 0)
C. The upper semicircle shifted down 1/3
D. The upper semicircle stretched: top (0, 9)

A. The upper semicircle compressed vertically: from (−3, 0) to (3, 0) with top (0, 1)

Multiplying by 1/3 compresses vertically: ends (±3, 0), top at (0, 1).

Outside × 1/3 = vertical compression.

Textbook Question · Problem 28

A. Stretch vertically by 2; the point (0, 1) moves to (0, 2)

y = 2H(x) has the form y = A·H(x − h) + k with A = 2, h = 0, k = 0. Stretch vertically by 2. A point (x, y) on the graph of H moves to (x + h, A·y + k): (0, 1) → (0, 2).

Inside the brackets (x ± c) moves the graph left/right in the opposite direction; outside changes move it up/down or stretch it.

Inside the brackets (x ± c) moves the graph left/right in the opposite direction; outside changes move it up/down or stretch it.

(d) Graph y = −f(x). Which description is correct?
A. Shift 1 unit right, then reflect across the x-axis; the point (3, 3) moves to (4, −3)
B. Reflect across the x-axis; the point (3, 3) moves to (3, −3)
C. No change; the point (3, 3) moves to (3, 3)
D. Reflect across the x-axis, then shift 1 unit up; the point (3, 3) moves to (3, −2)

B. Reflect across the x-axis; the point (3, 3) moves to (3, −3)

y = −f(x) has the form y = A·f(x − h) + k with A = −1, h = 0, k = 0. Reflect across the x-axis. A point (x, y) on the graph of f moves to (x + h, A·y + k): (3, 3) → (3, −3).

Inside the brackets (x ± c) moves the graph left/right in the opposite direction; outside changes move it up/down or stretch it.

Textbook Question · Problem 42
Same as Past Exam 2024 Question 5
Morphine, a pain-relieving drug, is administered to a patient intravenously starting at 8 am. The drug saturation curve Q = f(t) in Figure 1.81 gives the quantity, Q, of morphine in the blood t hours after 8 am.
a. Draw the drug saturation curve Q = g(t) if the IV line is started at noon instead of 8 am. Which description is correct?
A. The curve stretched vertically by 4
B. The same curve shifted 4 hours to the left
C. The same curve shifted 4 hours to the right: Q = 0 until t = 4, then rising toward 7.2
D. The same curve shifted 4 mg up

C. The same curve shifted 4 hours to the right: Q = 0 until t = 4, then rising toward 7.2

Starting at noon means everything happens 4 hours later: the curve is shifted 4 units to the right (it starts rising at t = 4).

Later start = shift right.

b. Is g one of the following transformations of f: vertical shift, vertical stretch, horizontal shift, horizontal stretch? If so, which?
A. Horizontal shift
B. Vertical shift
C. Vertical stretch
D. Horizontal stretch

A. Horizontal shift

It is a horizontal shift (4 hours to the right).

Time moves → horizontal.

c. Write g(t) in terms of the function f.
A. g(t) = f(t) + 4
B. g(t) = f(t − 4)
C. g(t) = 4f(t)
D. g(t) = f(t + 4)

B. g(t) = f(t − 4)

Shift right 4: g(t) = f(t − 4).

Right shift = minus inside.

Textbook Question · Problem 43
(a) Write an equation for a graph obtained by vertically stretching the graph of y = x² by a factor of 2, followed by a vertical upward shift of 1 unit.
A. y = 2(x² + 1) = 2x² + 2
B. y = 2(x + 1)²
C. y = 2x² + 1
D. y = (2x)² + 1

C. y = 2x² + 1

Stretch: 2x². Then up 1: y = 2x² + 1.

Stretch first, then add 1.

(b) What is the equation if the order of the transformations (stretching and shifting) in part (a) is interchanged?
A. y = 2x² + 1
B. y = (x + 1)²·2
C. y = 2x² + 0.5
D. y = 2(x² + 1) = 2x² + 2

D. y = 2(x² + 1) = 2x² + 2

Shift first: x² + 1. Then stretch by 2: y = 2(x² + 1) = 2x² + 2.

Now the 1 is also multiplied by 2.

(c) Are the two graphs the same? Explain the effect of reversing the order of transformations.
A. Yes: both are the same parabola
B. No: 2x² + 1 has vertex (0, 1) and 2x² + 2 has vertex (0, 2); the order matters
C. No: one opens upward and the other downward
D. Yes: the order of transformations never matters

B. No: 2x² + 1 has vertex (0, 1) and 2x² + 2 has vertex (0, 2); the order matters

2x² + 1 ≠ 2x² + 2. When the shift is done first, the stretch also doubles the shift, so the order matters.

Compare the vertices.

Past Exam Question · 2024 Q5
Same as Textbook Problem 42
A pain-relieving drug, called Morphine, is administered to a patient intravenously starting at 8 am. The drug saturation curve Q = f(t) in the figure below gives the quantity, Q, of morphine in the blood t hours after 8 am.
a. Sketch a new drug saturation curve Q = g(t) if the drug is administered at noon (12 pm) instead of 8 am. Which description is correct?
A. The curve stretched vertically by 4
B. The same curve shifted 4 hours to the left
C. The same curve shifted 4 mg up
D. The same curve shifted 4 hours to the right: Q = 0 until t = 4, then rising toward 7.2

D. The same curve shifted 4 hours to the right: Q = 0 until t = 4, then rising toward 7.2

Noon is 4 hours after 8 am: the curve shifts 4 units right.

Later start = shift right.

b. Write g(t) in terms of the function f(t).
A. g(t) = f(t − 4)
B. g(t) = f(t + 4)
C. g(t) = f(4t)
D. g(t) = f(t) − 4

g(t) = f(t − 4).

Right shift = minus inside.

Lecture 8Proportionality and Power Functions (1.9)

5 lecture · 30 textbook · 1 past exam questions

1. Proportionality2. Power Functions
📖 شرح المحاضرة — Proportionality and Power Functions (1.9)

الشرح فيه 3 أجزاء بنفس ترتيب الأسئلة: ① التناسب، ② دوال القوى، ③ شكل الرسمة. اقري الجزء، وبعدين حلي أسئلته.

1️⃣ التناسب (Proportionality)

"y يتناسب طردياً مع x" (y is proportional to x) يعني: لو x تضاعف، y يتضاعف معاه. مثل سعر الفلافل 🧆: كل ما زاد العدد، زاد السعر بنفس النسبة.

y = kx
  • k = ثابت التناسب (Constant of proportionality)، رقم ثابت ما يتغير.
  • كلمة "proportional to" = نكتب = k ×
  • إذا قال "proportional to the square root of l" ← T = k√l
  • إذا قال "proportional to the cube root of A" (الجذر التكعيبي) ← N = k∛A = kA1/3
🔑 طريقة الحل (دايماً 3 خطوات):
① اكتبي القانون y = k × (…) ← ② عوضي القيم اللي عطاج ياها واقسمي عشان تطلعين k ← ③ استخدمي k عشان تحسبين القيمة الجديدة
مثال (Ex 1): كتلة القلب H تتناسب مع كتلة الجسم B
i. H = kB

ii. إنسان كتلته 70 kg وقلبه 0.42 kg:

0.42 = k × 70
k = 0.42 / 70 = 0.006

iii. حصان كتلته 650 kg:

H = 0.006 × 650 = 3.9 kg
مثال (Ex 2): كتلة الدم تتناسب مع كتلة الجسم. وحيد القرن 3000 kg ودمه 150 kg
i. B = kM ← 150 = 3000k ← k = 150 / 3000 = 0.05
B = 0.05M

ii. إنسان 70 kg:

B = 0.05 × 70 = 3.5 kg
مثال (Past Exam 2022): نفس الفكرة، حصان 600 kg ودمه 30 kg
a. 30 = 600k ← k = 30 / 600 = 0.05 ← B = 0.05M
b. إنسان 80 kg: B = 0.05 × 80 = 4 kg
مثال (Ex 3): زمن البندول T يتناسب مع الجذر التربيعي لطوله l

زمن الدورة (Period) = الوقت اللي ياخذه البندول عشان يروح ويرجع مرة وحدة.

i. T = k√l

ii. بندول طوله 4 m وزمنه 10 ثواني:

10 = k√4 = 2k
k = 10 / 2 = 5

iii. بندول طوله 0.25 m:

T = 5√0.25 = 5 × 0.5 = 2.5 seconds
2️⃣ دوال القوى (Power Functions)

دالة القوة (Power function) شكلها:

y = k xp
  • k = المعامل (Coefficient)، الرقم اللي قدام.
  • p = الأس (Exponent)، الرقم اللي فوق.
  • لازم يكون x تحت (في القاعدة Base) والرقم الثابت فوق.
مثالدالة قوة؟
x تحت والأس رقمx³✅ Power
x فوق في الأس5.2ˣ❌ هذي أسية (Exponential)
فيها جمع رقم3x² + 4❌ مو بشكل kxᵖ

عشان نحولها لشكل kxᵖ، نحتاج قواعد الأسس (Exponent rules):

القاعدةمثال
1 / xⁿ = x−n1 / x³ = x−3
√x = x1/2∛x = x1/3
(ab)ⁿ = aⁿ bⁿ(3x)² = 9x²
(xm)n = xm×n(x²)³ = x⁶
🔑 إذا x تحت الكسر: طلعيها فوق وخلي أسها سالب. والأرقام اللي معاها تبقى كسر عادي:
2 / (3x) = (2/3) × (1/x) = (2/3) x−1
مثال (Ex 4) a–c: هل هي دالة قوة؟ اكتبيها y = kxᵖ
a) 5 / x³ = 5x−3 ← k = 5 ، p = −3
b) 2 / (3x) = (2/3)x−1 ← k = 2/3 ، p = −1
c) 5x² / 2 = (5/2)x² ← k = 5/2 ، p = 2
مثال (Ex 4) d–f
d) 5.2ˣ ← x فوق في الأس ← ❌ Not a power function (Exponential)
e) 3√x = 3x1/2 ← k = 3 ، p = 1/2

f) نوزع الأس 3 على الرقم وعلى x:

(3x²)³ = 3³ × (x²)³ = 27 × x6
y = 27x⁶ ← k = 27 ، p = 6
💡 ملاحظة: لو قال "inversely proportional" (يتناسب عكسياً) يعني x تنزل تحت: y = k / x = kx−1. يعني دالة قوة أسها سالب.
3️⃣ شكل رسمة دالة القوة (Shape of the Graph)

نحتاج كلمتين عن شكل المنحنى:

  • متزايدة (Increasing): الرسمة تطلع لفوق كل ما مشينا يمين ↗️
  • مقعرة للأعلى (Concave up): مثل الكوب ∪ 🥣، تطلع وتسرع أكثر وأكثر.
  • مقعرة للأسفل (Concave down): مثل القبة ∩، تطلع بس تبطئ شوي شوي.
الأس p (و k موجب، x موجب)الشكلمثال
p > 1Increasing و Concave upx²
p = 1خط مستقيمx
0 < p < 1Increasing و Concave down√x = x1/2
p < 0Decreasing (تنزل)1/x
🔑 الجذور (√ أو ∛) أسها بين 0 و 1 ← دايماً Increasing و Concave down.
مثال (Ex 5): عدد الأنواع N يتناسب مع الجذر التكعيبي لمساحة الجزيرة A
Cube root ← ∛A = A1/3
N = kA1/3
p = 1/3 ← 0 < 1/3 < 1
N = kA1/3 ← Increasing و Concave down

يعني: الجزيرة الأكبر فيها أنواع أكثر، بس الزيادة تبطئ كل ما كبرت المساحة.

🧠 كيف تعرفين نوع السؤال؟
إذا السؤال فيه…سوي
"proportional to"y = kx
"proportional to the square root"y = k√x
"proportional to the cube root"y = kx1/3
"inversely proportional"y = k / x
"find the constant of proportionality"عوضي القيمتين واقسمي ← k
"estimate" لقيمة جديدةحطي k والرقم الجديد بالقانون
"is it a power function?"x تحت والأس رقم؟ حوليها لـ kxᵖ
"describe the shape"شوفي p: بين 0 و 1 ← Concave down
⚠️ أخطاء شائعة:
• 2ˣ مو دالة قوة (x فوق)، بس x² دالة قوة.
• في (3x²)³ لا تنسين تكعبين الـ 3 بعد: 3³ = 27.
• 1 / x³ أسها −3 مو 3.
• لما تطلعين k، اقسمي القيمة المعطاة على الرقم اللي مع k (مثلاً 0.42 / 70).

✍️ جربي حلي الأسئلة تحت بزر Solve here، والحسابات بتطلع لك على طول.

1. Proportionality

4 lecture · 14 textbook · 1 past exam questions

Lecture Question · Ex 1
The heart mass of a mammal is proportional to its body mass.
i. Write a formula for heart mass, H, as a function of body mass, B.
A. H = kB²
B. H = kB
C. H = B + k
D. H = k/B

B. H = kB

Proportional → H = kB.

"Proportional to" = multiply by a constant.

ii. A human with a body mass of 70 kilograms has a heart mass of 0.42 kilograms. Use this information to find the constant of proportionality.
A. k = 0.006
B. k = 0.06
C. k = 29.4
D. k = 166.7

A. k = 0.006

0.42 = 70k → k = 0.42/70 = 0.006.

Divide 0.42 by 70.

iii. Estimate the heart mass of a horse with a body mass of 650 kg.
A. 39 kg
B. 0.39 kg
C. 4.2 kg
D. 3.9 kg

D. 3.9 kg

H = 0.006(650) = 3.9 kg.

Multiply by k.

Lecture Question · Ex 2
Same as Textbook Problem 22 (similar problem with different numbers: Past Exam 2022 Question 4)
The blood mass of a mammal is proportional to its body mass. A rhinoceros with body mass 3000 kilograms has blood mass of 150 kilograms.
i. Find a formula for the blood mass of a mammal as a function of the body mass.
A. B = 0.5M
B. B = 150M
C. B = 0.05M
D. B = 20M

C. B = 0.05M

150 = 3000k → k = 0.05 → B = 0.05M.

k = 150/3000.

ii. Estimate the blood mass of a human with body mass 70 kilograms.
A. 7 kg
B. 1400 kg
C. 3.5 kg
D. 35 kg

C. 3.5 kg

B = 0.05(70) = 3.5 kg.

Multiply by 0.05.

Lecture Question · Ex 3
The period of a pendulum, T, is the amount of time required for the pendulum to make one complete swing. For small swings, the period, T, is approximately proportional to the square root of l, the pendulum's length.
i. Write a formula for period, T, as a function of pendulum's length, l.
A. T = k√l
B. T = k/√l
C. T = kl²
D. T = kl

A. T = k√l

Proportional to the square root → T = k√l.

Square root of l times a constant.

ii. Calculate the proportionality constant k for a 4 meter pendulum with a period of 10 seconds.
A. k = 40
B. k = 20
C. k = 2.5
D. k = 5

D. k = 5

10 = k√4 = 2k → k = 5.

√4 = 2.

iii. Estimate the period T for a 0.25 meter pendulum.
A. T = 1.25 seconds
B. T = 2.5 seconds
C. T = 0.5 seconds
D. T = 10 seconds

B. T = 2.5 seconds

T = 5√0.25 = 5(0.5) = 2.5 seconds.

√0.25 = 0.5.

Lecture Question · Ex 5
If N is the average number of species found on an island and A is the area of the island, observations have shown that N is approximately proportional to the cube root of A.
Write a formula for N as a function of A and describe the shape of the graph of this function.
A. N = kA1/3; decreasing and concave up
B. N = kA1/3; increasing and concave down
C. N = k/A³; decreasing and concave up
D. N = kA³; increasing and concave up

B. N = kA1/3; increasing and concave down

Cube root → N = kA1/3. Since 0 < 1/3 < 1, the graph is increasing and concave down.

Powers between 0 and 1 rise and flatten.

Textbook Question · Problem 13
In Problems 13–16, write a formula representing the function.
The strength, S, of a beam is proportional to the square of its thickness, h.
A. S = k√h
B. S = kh
C. S = k/h²
D. S = kh²

D. S = kh²

S = kh².

"Proportional to" = multiply by a constant.

Textbook Question · Problem 14
Write a formula representing the function.
The energy, E, expended by a swimming dolphin is proportional to the cube of the speed, v, of the dolphin.
A. E = kv³
B. E = kv1/3
C. E = k/v³
D. E = 3kv

A. E = kv³

E = kv³.

"Proportional to" = multiply by a constant.

Textbook Question · Problem 15
Write a formula representing the function.
The average velocity, v, for a trip over a fixed distance, d, is inversely proportional to the time of travel, t.
A. v = t/k (k = d)
B. v = kt (k = d)
C. v = k/t (k = d)
D. v = k/t² (k = d)

C. v = k/t (k = d)

Inversely proportional → v = k/t, where k = d.

"Inversely proportional" = constant divided by the quantity.

Textbook Question · Problem 16
Write a formula representing the function.
The gravitational force, F, between two bodies is inversely proportional to the square of the distance d between them.
A. F = k/d
B. F = k/√d
C. F = kd²
D. F = k/d²

D. F = k/d²

F = k/d².

"Inversely proportional" = constant divided by the quantity.

Textbook Question · Problem 17
The number of species of lizards, N, found on an island off Baja California is proportional to the fourth root of the area, A, of the island.
Write a formula for N as a function of A. Graph this function. Is it increasing or decreasing? Is the graph concave up or concave down? What does this tell you about lizards and island area?
A. N = kA1/4; decreasing, concave up: larger islands have fewer species
B. N = kA1/4; increasing, concave down: more area gives more species, but gains slow down
C. N = k/A⁴; decreasing, concave up: larger islands have fewer species
D. N = kA⁴; increasing, concave up: more area gives more and more new species

B. N = kA1/4; increasing, concave down: more area gives more species, but gains slow down

N = kA1/4. Since 0 < 1/4 < 1, it is increasing and concave down: bigger islands have more lizard species, but the increase slows down as the area grows.

Root functions rise and flatten.

Textbook Question · Problem 18
The surface area of a mammal, S, satisfies the equation S = kM2/3, where M is the body mass, and the constant of proportionality k depends on the body shape of the mammal. A human of body mass 70 kilograms has surface area 18,600 cm².
Find the constant of proportionality for humans. Find the surface area of a human with body mass 60 kilograms.
A. k ≈ 265.7; S(60) ≈ 15,943 cm²
B. k ≈ 4.4; S(60) ≈ 67 cm²
C. k ≈ 1095; S(60) ≈ 16,783 cm²
D. k ≈ 1095; S(60) ≈ 15,943 cm²

C. k ≈ 1095; S(60) ≈ 16,783 cm²

k = 18,600/702/3 ≈ 1095. S(60) = 1095 · 602/3 ≈ 16,783 cm².

Find k first, then substitute 60.

Textbook Question · Problem 20
Kleiber's Law states that the metabolic needs (such as calorie requirements) of a mammal are proportional to its body weight raised to the 0.75 power. Surprisingly, the daily diets of mammals conform to this relation well. Assuming Kleiber's Law holds:
a. Write a formula for C, daily calorie consumption, as a function of body weight, W.
A. C = kW0.75
B. C = 0.75kW
C. C = k/W0.75
D. C = kW1.75

A. C = kW0.75

C = kW0.75.

Proportional to W to the 0.75 power.

b. Sketch a graph of this function. Which description is correct?
A. Increasing and concave down, starting at the origin
B. A straight line through the origin
C. Decreasing and concave up
D. Increasing and concave up, starting at the origin

A. Increasing and concave down, starting at the origin

0 < 0.75 < 1, so the graph rises from the origin and is concave down.

Power between 0 and 1.

c. If a human weighing 150 pounds needs to consume 1800 calories a day, estimate the daily calorie requirement of a horse weighing 700 lbs and of a rabbit weighing 9 lbs.
A. Horse ≈ 3200 calories; rabbit ≈ 218 calories
B. Horse ≈ 8400 calories; rabbit ≈ 108 calories
C. Horse ≈ 5715 calories; rabbit ≈ 108 calories
D. Horse ≈ 5715 calories; rabbit ≈ 218 calories

D. Horse ≈ 5715 calories; rabbit ≈ 218 calories

k = 1800/1500.75 ≈ 42.0. Horse: 42.0(700)0.75 ≈ 5715. Rabbit: 42.0(9)0.75 ≈ 218.

Find k from the human first.

d. On a per-pound basis, which animal requires more calories: a mouse or an elephant?
A. The elephant
B. The mouse
C. It cannot be decided
D. They need the same per pound

B. The mouse

Calories per pound = kW0.75/W = kW−0.25, which is larger for small W: the mouse.

Per pound: divide by W.

Textbook Question · Problem 21
Allometry is the study of the relative size of different parts of a body as a consequence of growth. In this problem, you will check the accuracy of an allometric equation: the weight of a fish is proportional to the cube of its length. Table 1.37 relates the weight, y, in gm, of plaice (a type of fish) to its length, x, in cm.
x33.534.535.536.537.538.5
y332363391419455500
x39.540.541.542.543.5
y538574623674724
Does this data support the hypothesis that (approximately) y = kx³? If so, estimate the constant of proportionality, k.
A. No, y/x³ is not close to constant
B. Yes, k ≈ 0.087
C. Yes, k ≈ 0.0087
D. Yes, k ≈ 9.9

C. Yes, k ≈ 0.0087

y/x³ for each column is about 0.0086–0.0088 (nearly constant), so yes, with k ≈ 0.0087.

Divide each y by x³.

Textbook Question · Problem 22
Same as Lecture Example 2 (similar problem with different numbers: Past Exam 2022 Question 4)
The blood mass of a mammal is proportional to its body mass. A rhinoceros with body mass 3000 kilograms has blood mass of 150 kilograms.
Find a formula for the blood mass of a mammal as a function of the body mass and estimate the blood mass of a human with body mass 70 kilograms.
A. B = 0.05M; B(70) = 35 kg
B. B = 20M; B(70) = 1400 kg
C. B = 0.5M; B(70) = 35 kg
D. B = 0.05M; B(70) = 3.5 kg

D. B = 0.05M; B(70) = 3.5 kg

k = 150/3000 = 0.05 → B = 0.05M; B(70) = 3.5 kg.

k = 150/3000.

Textbook Question · Problem 23
Biologists estimate that the number of animal species of a certain body length is inversely proportional to the square of the body length.
Write a formula for the number of animal species, N, of a certain body length as a function of the length, L. Are there more species at large lengths or at small lengths? Explain.
A. N = kL²; more species at small lengths
B. N = k/L²; more species at small lengths
C. N = k/L²; more species at large lengths
D. N = kL²; more species at large lengths

B. N = k/L²; more species at small lengths

N = k/L². As L increases, N decreases, so there are more species at small lengths.

Inversely: bigger L → smaller N.

Textbook Question · Problem 24
The specific heat, s, of an element is the number of calories of heat required to raise the temperature of one gram of the element by one degree Celsius.
ElementLiMgAlFeAgPbHg
w6.924.327.055.8107.9207.2200.6
s0.920.250.210.110.0560.0310.033
Use the table to decide if s is proportional or inversely proportional to the atomic weight, w, of the element. If so, find the constant of proportionality.
A. Inversely proportional, k ≈ 6
B. Inversely proportional, k ≈ 0.16
C. Neither
D. Proportional, k ≈ 0.13

A. Inversely proportional, k ≈ 6

s·w ≈ 6.35, 6.08, 5.67, 6.14, 6.04, 6.42, 6.62 — roughly constant ≈ 6. So s ≈ 6/w: inversely proportional with k ≈ 6.

Multiply s by w.

Textbook Question · Problem 25
The circulation time of a mammal (that is, the average time it takes for all the blood in the body to circulate once and return to the heart) is proportional to the fourth root of the body mass of the mammal.
a. Write a formula for the circulation time, T, in terms of the body mass, B.
A. T = kB⁴
B. T = (kB)⁴
C. T = kB1/4
D. T = k/B1/4

C. T = kB1/4

T = kB1/4.

Fourth root = power 1/4.

b. If an elephant of body mass 5230 kilograms has a circulation time of 148 seconds, find the constant of proportionality.
A. k ≈ 17.4
B. k ≈ 35.3
C. k ≈ 8.5
D. k ≈ 0.028

A. k ≈ 17.4

k = 148/52301/4 ≈ 148/8.504 ≈ 17.4.

Lecture 9Periodic Functions (1.10)

7 lecture · 32 textbook · 3 past exam questions

1. Periodic Data & Graphs2. Sine & Cosine: Amplitude, Period & Shifts3. Finding Formulas for Periodic Functions
📖 شرح المحاضرة — Periodic Functions (1.10)

المحاضرة عن الأشياء اللي تتكرر بنفس النمط، مثل حرارة اليوم أو التنفس أو ضغط الدم. الشرح فيه 3 أجزاء بنفس ترتيب الأسئلة. اقري الجزء، وبعدين حلي أسئلته.

1️⃣ البيانات الدورية والرسمة (Periodic Data & Graphs)

الدالة الدورية (Periodic function) = رسمة تعيد نفسها كل فترة. مثل موج البحر 🌊: يطلع وينزل، يطلع وينزل.

نحتاج 3 كلمات:

  • الدورة (Period) = كم وقت ياخذ النمط عشان يتكرر مرة وحدة كاملة. (مثلاً من قمة لين القمة اللي بعدها)
  • خط المنتصف (Midline) = الخط اللي بالنص بالضبط، بين أعلى نقطة وأوطى نقطة.
  • السعة (Amplitude) = المسافة من خط المنتصف لين القمة. يعني "كم تطلع الموجة فوق النص".
Amplitude = (max − min) / 2
Midline = (max + min) / 2
📈 كيف تقرين الرسمة:
① دوري أعلى نقطة (max) وأوطى نقطة (min) على المحور العمودي.
② دوري قمتين ورا بعض، واطرحي وقتهم ← هذا الـ Period.
🔑 عشان تعرفين القيمة بوقت ما يبين بالرسمة: زيدي أو انقصي Periods كاملة لين توصلين وقت موجود بالرسمة. القيمة نفسها لأن النمط يتكرر.
مثال (Ex 1): حرارة الفريزر المسكّر

من الرسمة: الحرارة تتراوح بين −3°F و 2°F، وفيه قمة عند 1:20 والقمة اللي بعدها عند 1:45.

i. Amplitude = (2 − (−3)) / 2 = 5 / 2 = 2.5°F
Period = 1:45 − 1:20 = 25 minutes

ii. الساعة 12:30 مو بالرسمة. نرجع من القمة 1:20 بـ Period ين (50 دقيقة):

1:20 − 2 × 25 min = 12:30 ← قمة بعد ← ≈ 2°F

iii. الساعة 2:45: ننقص Period ين:

2:45 − 2 × 25 min = 1:55
عند 1:55 الرسمة تقريباً −1.5°F ← ≈ −1.5°F
2️⃣ الساين والكوساين (Sine & Cosine: Amplitude, Period & Shifts)

أشهر دالتين دوريتين: sin t و cos t. هني t بالـ راديان (Radians)، و π ≈ 3.14 مجرد رقم.

t0π/2π3π/22π
sin t010−10
cos t10−101
  • sin t: يبدا من النص (0) ويطلع لفوق.
  • cos t: يبدا من القمة (1) وينزل.
  • الاثنين بين −1 و 1 ← Amplitude = 1، و Period = 2π.

الشكل العام:

y = D + A sin(Bt)    أو    y = D + A cos(Bt)
الرمزمعناهتأثيره على الرسمة
AAmplitudeيطول الموجة أو يقصرها
Bيحدد الـ PeriodPeriod = 2π / B
DMidlineيرفع الموجة أو ينزلها
🔑 B كبير ← Period صغير (الموج يتزاحم 🌀). مثلاً sin 2t تعيد نفسها مرتين أسرع من sin t.
مثال (Ex 2): y = 3 sin 2t، كم الـ Amplitude والـ Period؟
A = 3 ← الرسمة بين −3 و 3
B = 2 ← Period = 2π / 2 = π
Amplitude 3 ، Period π
مثال (Ex 3): من رسمة sin t ارسمي
i. y = 2 sin t ← A = 2 ← بين −2 و 2، والـ Period نفسه 2π
ii. y = sin t + 3 ← D = 3 ← ترتفع 3: بين 2 و 4، والـ Period نفسه 2π

لاحظي: نفس قواعد المحاضرة اللي قبل. الضرب برا = تمدد، والجمع برا = فوق.

مثال (Ex 4): شنو الفرق بينها وبين y = sin t؟
(a) 6 sin t ← Amplitude 6 بدال 1 (تمدد عمودي)، نفس الـ Period
(b) 5 + sin t ← تطلع فوق 5: Midline صار 5، والرسمة بين 4 و 6

(c) هني الرقم داخل القوس، يعني يمين/يسار بعكس الإشارة:

(c) sin(t + π/2) ← يسار π/2 ، وتصير نفس رسمة cos t
مثال (Ex 5): شنو تأثير A و B؟
(a) y = A sin t ← A هو الـ Amplitude: كل ما كبر، الموجة أطول. الـ Period ما يتغير (2π)
(b) y = sin(Bt) ← Period = 2π / B: كل ما كبر B، الـ Period أقصر (موج أكثر). الـ Amplitude يبقى 1
3️⃣ نطلع القانون من الرسمة أو الجدول (Finding Formulas)
🔑 4 خطوات:
① D = (max + min) / 2
② A = (max − min) / 2
③ B = 2π / Period
④ شوفي الرسمة عند t = 0 وين تبدا، واختاري من الجدول تحت 👇
عند t = 0 الرسمة…استخدمي
على خط المنتصف وتطلع ↗️+ A sin
على خط المنتصف وتنزل ↘️− A sin
عند القمة (max) 🔝+ A cos
عند القاع (min) ⬇️− A cos
مثال (Ex 6) i: رسمة g(t)

من الرسمة: تبدا من 0 وتطلع، أعلى نقطة 3 وأوطى −3، وتكمل دورة وحدة عند 12π.

تبدا من النص وتطلع ← sin
D = 0 ، A = 3
B = 2π / 12π = 1/6
g(t) = 3 sin(t/6)
مثال (Ex 6) ii: رسمة h(t)

من الرسمة: تبدا من القمة 700، أوطى نقطة 300، والـ Period = 12.

تبدا من القمة ← cos
D = (700 + 300) / 2 = 500 ، A = (700 − 300) / 2 = 200
B = 2π / 12 = π/6
h(t) = 500 + 200 cos(πt/6)
مثال (Ex 7): من الجدول، أعلى قيمة 5
x024681012
f(x)50−5050−5
i. بين −5 و 5 ← Amplitude = 5
ii. f(0) = 5 ورجعت 5 عند x = 8 ← Period = 8
iii. تبدا من القمة ← cos ، B = 2π / 8 = π/4
f(x) = 5 cos(πx/4)
مثال (Past Exam) ⭐: عدد الثعالب N

من الرسمة: بين 10 و 70، تبدا من 40 وتنزل أول، وتتكرر كل 6 شهور.

D = (70 + 10) / 2 = 40 ، A = (70 − 10) / 2 = 30
تبدا من النص وتنزل ← −sin
B = 2π / 6 = π/3
i. N = 40 − 30 sin(πt/3)

ii. بعد 24 شهر، نعوض t = 24:

(π/3) × 24 = 8π ← sin(8π) = 0
N = 40 − 30 × 0 = 40 foxes

منطقي: 24 شهر = 4 Periods كاملة بالضبط، فرجعنا لنفس نقطة البداية (40).

مثال (Past Exam 2024): ضغط الدم P

من الرسمة: بين 80 و 120، تبدا من القاع عند t = 0، والـ Period = 3 ثواني.

D = (120 + 80) / 2 = 100 ، A = (120 − 80) / 2 = 20
تبدا من القاع ← −cos
B = 2π / 3
P = 100 − 20 cos(2πt/3)
🧠 كيف تعرفين نوع السؤال؟
إذا السؤال فيه…سوي
"amplitude"(max − min) / 2
"period" من رسمة أو جدولالوقت من قمة لين القمة اللي بعدها
"period" من قانون2π / B
"estimate the value at" وقت برا الرسمةزيدي/انقصي Periods كاملة
"how does it differ from sin t"A ← طول، B ← Period، D ← فوق/تحت، داخل القوس ← يمين/يسار
"find a possible formula"الخطوات الأربع: D، A، B، وبعدين sin أو cos
"predict after 24 months"عوضي t بالقانون
⚠️ أخطاء شائعة:
• الـ Amplitude نص المسافة بين max و min، مو المسافة كلها.
• B = 2π / Period، مو Period نفسه.
• اختاري sin أو cos من نقطة البداية عند t = 0، ولا تنسين السالب إذا تبدا تنزل أو من القاع.
• الآلة الحاسبة لازم تكون على Radian (RAD) مو Degree.

✍️ جربي حلي الأسئلة تحت بزر Solve here، والحسابات بتطلع لك على طول.

1. Periodic Data & Graphs

1 lecture · 6 textbook questions

Lecture Question · Ex 1
Figure 1.89 shows the temperature in an unopened "closed" freezer.
i. Estimate the amplitude and the period.
A. Amplitude 5°F, period 25 minutes
B. Amplitude 2°F, period 20 minutes
C. Amplitude 2.5°F, period 50 minutes
D. Amplitude 2.5°F, period 25 minutes

D. Amplitude 2.5°F, period 25 minutes

Temperature goes between −3°F and 2°F: amplitude = (2 − (−3))/2 = 2.5°F. One cycle (e.g. 1:20 to 1:45) takes 25 minutes.

Amplitude = half of (max − min).

ii. Estimate the temperature in the freezer at 12:30.
A. ≈ −1.5°F
B. ≈ 0°F
C. ≈ 2°F
D. ≈ −3°F

C. ≈ 2°F

Go back from 1:20 (a peak, 2°F) by whole periods: 1:20 − 2(25 min) = 12:30 is also a peak: ≈ 2°F.

Use the period to go back in time.

iii. Estimate the temperature in the freezer at 2:45.
A. ≈ 2°F
B. ≈ −1.5°F
C. ≈ −3°F
D. ≈ 1°F

B. ≈ −1.5°F

2:45 − 2(25 min) = 1:55, where the graph is at about −1.5°F.

Use the period to move into the graph.

Textbook Question · Problem 1
A graduate student in environmental science studied the temperature fluctuations of a river. Figure 1.99 shows the temperature of the river (in °C) every hour, with hour 0 being midnight of the first day.
a. Explain why a periodic function could be used to model these data.
A. The pattern repeats every day
B. The temperature is constant
C. The temperature keeps increasing
D. The pattern never repeats

A. The pattern repeats every day

The temperature rises and falls in the same pattern every day.

Repeating pattern = periodic.

b. Approximately when does the maximum occur? The minimum? Why does this make sense?
A. Maximum at noon; minimum at midnight (exactly)
B. Maximum ≈ 8 am; minimum ≈ 9 pm
C. Maximum ≈ 9 am; minimum ≈ 8 pm (water cools during the day)
D. Maximum ≈ 8 pm; minimum ≈ 9 am (water warms during the day and cools at night)

D. Maximum ≈ 8 pm; minimum ≈ 9 am (water warms during the day and cools at night)

Peaks are around hours 20, 44, 68, 92 (≈ 8 pm); lows around 9 am. The water warms during the day and cools at night.

Read the hours of the peaks.

c. What is the period for these data? What is the amplitude?
A. Period ≈ 24 hours; amplitude ≈ 3.5°C
B. Period ≈ 24 hours; amplitude ≈ 1.75°C
C. Period ≈ 48 hours; amplitude ≈ 31.75°C
D. Period ≈ 12 hours; amplitude ≈ 1.75°C

B. Period ≈ 24 hours; amplitude ≈ 1.75°C

The pattern repeats every ≈ 24 hours; max ≈ 31.75, min ≈ 28.25 → amplitude ≈ 1.75°C.

Amplitude = half of (max − min).

Textbook Question · Problem 2
Figure 1.100 shows quarterly beer production during the period 1997 to 1999. Quarter 1 reflects production during the first three months of the year, etc.
a. Explain why a periodic function should be used to model these data.
A. The pattern repeats every year
B. Production keeps increasing
C. Production is constant
D. Production never repeats

A. The pattern repeats every year

The same pattern repeats every year.

Repeating pattern = periodic.

b. Approximately when does the maximum occur? The minimum? Why does this make sense?
A. Maximum in quarter 4; minimum in quarter 2
B. Maximum in quarter 1; minimum in quarter 3
C. Maximum in quarter 2; minimum in quarter 4
D. Maximum in quarter 3; minimum in quarter 1

C. Maximum in quarter 2; minimum in quarter 4

Each year production peaks in quarter 2 (spring/early summer, to supply summer demand) and is lowest in quarter 4.

Find the high and low point in each year.

c. What are the period and amplitude for these data?
A. Period 2 quarters; amplitude ≈ 5.5 million barrels
B. Period 4 quarters (1 year); amplitude ≈ 5.5 million barrels
C. Period 12 quarters; amplitude ≈ 49.5 million barrels
D. Period 4 quarters (1 year); amplitude ≈ 11 million barrels

B. Period 4 quarters (1 year); amplitude ≈ 5.5 million barrels

Repeats every 4 quarters; max ≈ 55, min ≈ 44 → amplitude ≈ 5.5 million barrels.

Half of max − min.

Textbook Question · Problem 3
Sketch a possible graph of sales of sunscreen in the northeastern US over a 3-year period, as a function of months since January 1 of the first year.
Explain why your graph should be periodic. What is the period?
A. Sales keep increasing every month; period 1 month
B. Sales repeat every 3 years; period 36 months
C. Sales repeat each year (high in summer, low in winter); period 12 months
D. Sales are highest in winter; period 6 months

C. Sales repeat each year (high in summer, low in winter); period 12 months

Sunscreen sales rise every summer and fall every winter, repeating each year: period 12 months.

Seasons repeat yearly.

Textbook Question · Problem 10
Values of a function are given in the following table.
t2025303540
f(t)1.81.41.72.32.0
t45505560
f(t)1.81.41.72.3
Period/amplitude Explain why this function appears to be periodic. Approximately what are the period and amplitude of the function?
A. The values repeat every 25 units: period ≈ 25; amplitude ≈ 0.45
B. The values repeat every 5 units: period ≈ 5; amplitude ≈ 0.45
C. The values repeat every 50 units: period ≈ 50; amplitude ≈ 2.3
D. The values repeat every 25 units: period ≈ 25; amplitude ≈ 0.9

A. The values repeat every 25 units: period ≈ 25; amplitude ≈ 0.45

f(20) = f(45) = 1.8, f(25) = f(50) = 1.4, … so period ≈ 25. Max 2.3, min 1.4 → amplitude ≈ 0.45.

Find when the values start again.

Values Assuming that the function is periodic, estimate its value at t = 15, at t = 75, and at t = 135.
A. f(15) ≈ 2.3, f(75) ≈ 1.7, f(135) ≈ 2.0
B. f(15) ≈ 1.4, f(75) ≈ 2.0, f(135) ≈ 1.8
C. f(15) ≈ 1.8, f(75) ≈ 2.3, f(135) ≈ 1.4
D. f(15) ≈ 2.0, f(75) ≈ 1.4, f(135) ≈ 2.3

D. f(15) ≈ 2.0, f(75) ≈ 1.4, f(135) ≈ 2.3

15 + 25 = 40 → 2.0; 75 − 25 = 50 → 1.4; 135 − 100 = 35 → 2.3.

Add or subtract the period 25.

Textbook Question · Problem 12
Figure 1.101 shows the levels of the hormones estrogen and progesterone during the monthly ovarian cycles in females.
Is the level of both hormones periodic? What is the period in each case? Approximately when in the monthly cycle is estrogen at a peak? Approximately when is progesterone at a peak?
A. Yes; period 56 days. Both peak around day 28
B. Yes; period 14 days. Estrogen peaks around day 20; progesterone around day 12
C. No, only estrogen is periodic; estrogen peaks around day 12
D. Yes; period 28 days. Estrogen peaks around day 12; progesterone around day 20

D. Yes; period 28 days. Estrogen peaks around day 12; progesterone around day 20

Both repeat every 28 days. Estrogen peaks around day 12 (before ovulation) and progesterone around day 20.

The pattern repeats each month.

Textbook Question · Problem 31
Table 1.40 gives values for g(t), a periodic function.
t02468101214
g(t)1419171513111419
t16182022242628
g(t)17151311141917
a. Estimate the period and amplitude for this function.
A. Period 24; amplitude 19
B. Period 12; amplitude 4
C. Period 12; amplitude 8
D. Period 6; amplitude 4

B. Period 12; amplitude 4

g(0) = g(12) = g(24) = 14 and the pattern repeats: period 12. Max 19, min 11 → amplitude 4.

Find where the values repeat.

b. Estimate g(34) and g(60).
A. g(34) = 11, g(60) = 14
B. g(34) = 14, g(60) = 11
C. g(34) = 19, g(60) = 17
D. g(34) = 13, g(60) = 19

A. g(34) = 11, g(60) = 14

g(34) = g(34 − 24) = g(10) = 11; g(60) = g(0) = 14.

Subtract whole periods.

2. Sine & Cosine: Amplitude, Period & Shifts

4 lecture · 8 textbook questions

Lecture Question · Ex 2
Use a graph of y = 3 sin 2t to estimate the amplitude and period of this function.
Amplitude and period?
A. Amplitude 3, period 2π
B. Amplitude 2, period 3π
C. Amplitude 3, period π
D. Amplitude 6, period π/2

C. Amplitude 3, period π

The graph goes from −3 to 3 (amplitude 3) and repeats every π (period 2π/2 = π).

Period = 2π/B.

Lecture Question · Ex 3
Use the graph of y = sin t to sketch the graphs of
i. y = 2 sin t
A. The sine wave stretched vertically: between −2 and 2, period 2π
B. The sine wave shifted up 2: between 1 and 3
C. The sine wave shifted 2 right
D. The sine wave with period π: between −1 and 1

A. The sine wave stretched vertically: between −2 and 2, period 2π

Multiplying by 2 doubles the amplitude: it oscillates between −2 and 2 with the same period 2π.

Outside × 2 = taller.

ii. y = sin t + 3
A. The sine wave shifted 3 left
B. The sine wave with period 3: between −1 and 1
C. The sine wave stretched by 3: between −3 and 3
D. The sine wave shifted up 3: between 2 and 4, period 2π

D. The sine wave shifted up 3: between 2 and 4, period 2π

Adding 3 shifts the graph up 3: it oscillates between 2 and 4, period 2π.

Outside + 3 = up 3.

Lecture Question · Ex 4
Explain how the graphs of each of the following functions differ from the graph of y = sin t.
(a) y = 6 sin t
A. Shifted 6 units right
B. Amplitude is 6 instead of 1 (vertical stretch); same period
C. Shifted up 6
D. Period is 6 instead of 2π

B. Amplitude is 6 instead of 1 (vertical stretch); same period

y = 6 sin t has amplitude 6 (it oscillates between −6 and 6); the period is still 2π.

Coefficient in front = amplitude.

(b) y = 5 + sin t
A. Shifted 5 units left
B. Amplitude 5
C. Shifted up 5 (oscillates between 4 and 6); same amplitude and period
D. Period 5

C. Shifted up 5 (oscillates between 4 and 6); same amplitude and period

Adding 5 moves the midline from 0 to 5: the graph oscillates between 4 and 6.

Constant added = midline.

(c) y = sin(t + π/2)
A. Shifted π/2 to the right
B. Amplitude π/2
C. Shifted π/2 to the left (it is the graph of cos t)
D. Shifted up π/2

C. Shifted π/2 to the left (it is the graph of cos t)

t + π/2 inside shifts the graph π/2 units left; sin(t + π/2) = cos t.

Inside + = left.

Lecture Question · Ex 5
(a) Graph y = A sin t for several positive values of A. Describe the effect of A on the graph.
A. A is the amplitude: larger A gives a taller wave; the period stays 2π
B. A is the period: larger A gives a longer wave
C. A shifts the graph up by A
D. A shifts the graph right by A

A. A is the amplitude: larger A gives a taller wave; the period stays 2π

For y = A sin t the wave goes between −A and A: A is the amplitude (larger A → taller wave). The period does not change.

A stretches vertically.

(b) Graph y = sin(Bt) for several positive values of B. Describe the effect of B on the graph.
A. B shifts the graph left by B
B. Period = 2π/B: larger B gives a shorter period (more waves)
C. Amplitude = B: larger B gives a taller wave
D. Period = 2πB: larger B gives a longer period

B. Period = 2π/B: larger B gives a shorter period (more waves)

For y = sin(Bt) the period is 2π/B: larger B squeezes the wave (shorter period); the amplitude stays 1.

B squeezes horizontally.

Textbook Question · Problem 4
For Problems 4–9, sketch graphs of the functions. What are their amplitudes and periods?
y = 3 sin x
A. Amplitude 3, period π
B. Amplitude 6, period 2π
C. Amplitude 1, period 6π
D. Amplitude 3, period 2π

D. Amplitude 3, period 2π

A = 3; period 2π/1 = 2π.

Amplitude = |A|; period = 2π/B.

Textbook Question · Problem 5
Sketch the graph. What are its amplitude and period?
y = 3 sin 2x
A. Amplitude 3, period π
B. Amplitude 3, period 2π
C. Amplitude 2, period 3π
D. Amplitude 6, period π/2

A. Amplitude 3, period π

A = 3; period 2π/2 = π.

Amplitude = |A|; period = 2π/B.

Textbook Question · Problem 6
Sketch the graph. What are its amplitude and period?
y = −3 sin 2θ
A. Amplitude −3, period π
B. Amplitude 3, period 2π
C. Amplitude 3, period π
D. Amplitude 3, period 4π

C. Amplitude 3, period π

Amplitude |−3| = 3 (the minus sign reflects the graph); period 2π/2 = π.

Amplitude = |A|; period = 2π/B.

Textbook Question · Problem 7
Sketch the graph. What are its amplitude and period?
y = 4 cos 2x
A. Amplitude 4, period 2π
B. Amplitude 4, period π
C. Amplitude 2, period 4π
D. Amplitude 8, period π

B. Amplitude 4, period π

A = 4; period 2π/2 = π.

Amplitude = |A|; period = 2π/B.

Textbook Question · Problem 8
Sketch the graph. What are its amplitude and period?
y = 4 cos(½t)
A. Amplitude ½, period 8π
B. Amplitude 4, period π
C. Amplitude 2, period 4π
D. Amplitude 4, period 4π

D. Amplitude 4, period 4π

A = 4; period 2π/(½) = 4π.

Amplitude = |A|; period = 2π/B.

Textbook Question · Problem 9
Sketch the graph. What are its amplitude and period?
y = 5 − sin 2t
A. Amplitude 4, period 2π
B. Amplitude 1, period π
C. Amplitude 5, period π
D. Amplitude 1, period 2π

B. Amplitude 1, period π

Amplitude |−1| = 1 (midline y = 5); period 2π/2 = π.

Amplitude = |A|; period = 2π/B.

Textbook Question · Problem 14
A person breathes in and out every three seconds. The volume of air in the person's lungs varies between a minimum of 2 liters and a maximum of 4 liters.
Which of the following is the best formula for the volume of air in the person's lungs as a function of time?
A. y = 2 + 2 sin(2πt/3)
B. y = 2 + 2 sin(πt/3)
C. y = 3 + sin(2πt/3)
D. y = 3 + sin(πt/3)

C. y = 3 + sin(2πt/3)

Midline (2 + 4)/2 = 3, amplitude 1, period 3 → B = 2π/3: y = 3 + sin(2πt/3). (Option (b) in the booklet.)

Midline = average of max and min.

Textbook Question · Problem 32
The Bay of Fundy in Canada has the largest tides in the world. The difference between low and high water levels is 15 meters (nearly 50 feet). At a particular point the depth of the water, y meters, is given as a function of time, t, in hours since midnight by y = D + A cos(B(t − C)).
a. What is the physical meaning of D?
A. The time of high tide
B. The difference between high and low water
C. The depth at high tide
D. The average water depth

D. The average water depth

D is the midline: the average water depth.

D is the middle level.

b. What is the value of A?
A. A = 7.5 m
B. A = 30 m
C. A = 12.4 m
D. A = 15 m

A. A = 7.5 m

The difference between high and low is 15 m, so A = 15/2 = 7.5 m.

Half the total range.

c. What is the value of B? Assume the time between successive high tides is 12.4 hours.
A. B ≈ 0.081
B. B ≈ 12.4
C. B ≈ 1.97
D. B ≈ 0.507

D. B ≈ 0.507

Period 12.4 = 2π/B → B = 2π/12.4 ≈ 0.507.

B = 2π / period.

d. What is the physical meaning of C?
A. The amplitude of the tide
B. The time of a high tide
C. The average water depth
D. The time between two high tides

B. The time of a high tide

cos is maximum when t − C = 0, so C is the time of a high tide.

cos starts at its maximum.

3. Finding Formulas for Periodic Functions

2 lecture · 18 textbook · 3 past exam questions

Lecture Question · Ex 6
Find possible formulas for the following periodic functions:
i. g(t)
A. g(t) = 3 sin(t/6)
B. g(t) = 6 sin(t/3)
C. g(t) = 3 cos(t/6)
D. g(t) = 3 sin(6t)

A. g(t) = 3 sin(t/6)

Starts at 0 going up → sine. Amplitude 3. Period 12π → B = 2π/12π = 1/6. g(t) = 3 sin(t/6).

B = 2π / period.

ii. h(t)
A. h(t) = 500 + 200 cos(πt/12)
B. h(t) = 500 + 200 sin(πt/6)
C. h(t) = 500 + 200 cos(πt/6)
D. h(t) = 700 cos(πt/6)

C. h(t) = 500 + 200 cos(πt/6)

Starts at the maximum → cosine. Midline 500, amplitude 200, period 12 → B = π/6. h(t) = 500 + 200 cos(πt/6).

Max at t = 0 → cosine.

Lecture Question · Ex 7
Same as Textbook Problem 11
The following table shows values of a periodic function f(x). The maximum value attained by the function is 5.
x024681012
f(x)50−5050−5
i. What is the amplitude of the function?
A. 10
B. 5
C. 2.5
D. 0

B. 5

The function goes between −5 and 5: amplitude 5.

Half of (max − min).

ii. What is the period of the function?
A. 2
B. 12
C. 8
D. 4

C. 8

f(0) = 5 and f(8) = 5 again (one full cycle): period 8.

When does it start again?

iii. Find a formula for this periodic function.
A. f(x) = 5 sin(πx/4)
B. f(x) = 5 cos(πx/8)
C. f(x) = 5 cos(4x)
D. f(x) = 5 cos(πx/4)

D. f(x) = 5 cos(πx/4)

Starts at the maximum → cosine. A = 5, period 8 → B = 2π/8 = π/4. f(x) = 5 cos(πx/4).

B = 2π / period.

Past Exam Question · Past Exam (Lecture)
Same as Past Exam 2022 Question 6
The number of foxes is a periodic function of time as shown in the figure below.
i. Find a possible formula for the number of foxes, N, in terms of time t (in months).
A. N = 40 − 30 sin(πt/3)
B. N = 40 − 30 cos(πt/3)
C. N = 40 + 30 sin(πt/3)
D. N = 40 − 30 sin(πt/6)

A. N = 40 − 30 sin(πt/3)

Midline 40 (between 10 and 70), amplitude 30. It starts at 40 and goes down first → −sin. Period 6 months → B = 2π/6 = π/3. N = 40 − 30 sin(πt/3).

Starts at the midline going down → negative sine.

ii. Predict the number of foxes after 24 months.
A. 24 foxes
B. 40 foxes
C. 10 foxes
D. 70 foxes

B. 40 foxes

N(24) = 40 − 30 sin(8π) = 40 − 0 = 40 foxes (24 months is exactly 4 periods).

24 is a multiple of the period 6.

f(0) = 5 and f(8) = 5 again (one full cycle): period 8.

Textbook Question · Problem 13
Average daily high temperatures in Ottawa, the capital of Canada, range from a low of −6° Celsius on January 1 to a high of 26° Celsius on July 1 six months later. See Figure 1.102.
Find a formula for H, the average daily high temperature in Ottawa, in °C, as a function of t, the number of months since January 1.
A. H = 10 − 16 cos(πt/6)
B. H = 10 + 16 cos(πt/6)
C. H = 10 − 16 sin(πt/6)
D. H = 10 − 16 cos(πt/12)

A. H = 10 − 16 cos(πt/6)

Midline (26 + (−6))/2 = 10, amplitude 16, period 12 → B = π/6. Minimum at t = 0 → −cos. H = 10 − 16 cos(πt/6).

Minimum at t = 0 → negative cosine.

Textbook Question · Problem 15
Delta Cephei is one of the most visible stars in the night sky. Its brightness has periods of 5.4 days, the average brightness is 4.0 and its brightness varies by ±0.35.
Find a formula that models the brightness of Delta Cephei as a function of time, t, with t = 0 at peak brightness.
A. B = 4.0 + 0.35 sin(2πt/5.4)
B. B = 4.0 + 0.35 cos(2πt/5.4)
C. B = 0.35 + 4.0 cos(2πt/5.4)
D. B = 4.0 + 0.35 cos(5.4t)

B. B = 4.0 + 0.35 cos(2πt/5.4)

Peak at t = 0 → cosine. Midline 4.0, amplitude 0.35, period 5.4 → B = 2π/5.4.

Peak at t = 0 → cosine.

Textbook Question · Problem 16
Most breeding birds in the northeast US migrate elsewhere during the winter. The number of bird species in an Ohio forest preserve oscillates between a high of 28 in June and a low of 10 in December.
a. Graph the number of bird species as a function of t, the number of months since June (at least three years). Which description is correct?
A. Starts at 10, rises to 28 at t = 6, repeating every 12 months
B. Starts at 28 and decreases steadily
C. Starts at 28 (t = 0), falls to 10 at t = 6, back to 28 at t = 12, repeating
D. Starts at 19, rises to 28 at t = 3

C. Starts at 28 (t = 0), falls to 10 at t = 6, back to 28 at t = 12, repeating

June is t = 0 (high 28), December t = 6 (low 10), June again t = 12 (28).

Start at the high in June.

b. What are the amplitude and period of this function?
A. Amplitude 18; period 12 months
B. Amplitude 19; period 12 months
C. Amplitude 9; period 6 months
D. Amplitude 9; period 12 months

D. Amplitude 9; period 12 months

Amplitude (28 − 10)/2 = 9; period 12 months.

Half of (max − min).

c. Find a formula for the number of bird species, B, as a function of the number of months, t, since June.
A. B = 19 − 9 cos(πt/6)
B. B = 9 + 19 cos(πt/6)
C. B = 19 + 9 cos(πt/6)
D. B = 19 + 9 sin(πt/6)

C. B = 19 + 9 cos(πt/6)

Midline 19, amplitude 9, period 12 → B = π/6; maximum at t = 0 → cosine.

Max at t = 0 → cosine.

Textbook Question · Problem 17
For Problems 17–28, find a possible formula for each graph.
Formula = ?
A. y = 7 cos(πt/5)
B. y = 7 sin(πt/10)
C. y = −7 sin(πt/5)
D. y = 7 sin(πt/5)

D. y = 7 sin(πt/5)

Midline, amplitude, period (B = 2π/period), then sine or cosine from the starting point.

Textbook Question · Problem 18
